articles.title: Pranab Mukherjee hinted at desire to become PM, ‘shocked’ me, writes Sonia Gandhi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: In her memoir, former Congress president recalls 2010 conversation; Pranab Mukherjee’s daughter Sharmistha asks what there was to be shocked about, says it is not a crime to be ambitious

Former President Pranab Mukherjee had “shocked” Sonia Gandhi by hinting at his “long-held desire” to become Prime Minister during a conversation with her in 2010, suggesting that perhaps it was time for a “change at the top”, the former Congress president has written in her memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love .
The book, published by HarperCollins, was made available in bookstores on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), but the official launch is likely to take place on November 16.

Mukherjee, then a senior member of the Manmohan Singh Cabinet, had developed serious differences with the then Finance Minister P. Chidambaram. He would sometimes stay back for conversations with Ms. Gandhi after meetings of the Congress Strategy Group, which was set up to discuss parliamentary business.

“On one occasion, in 2010, I think after expressing his frustration, he shocked me with the suggestion that perhaps it was time for a change at the top, which I understood as a hint of his long-held desire to become Prime Minister,” she wrote.
“I gently changed the subject, and though he may have been disappointed, he never made me feel he held it against me,” she added.

The late Mukherjee, who had served in Indira Gandhi’s Cabinet in the 1970s, was part of a core group that met weekly with Dr. Singh to coordinate the functioning of the government and the party. Other members included Arjun Singh, A.K. Antony and Ahmed Patel.
Ms. Gandhi says she often called on Mukherjee after he became President in 2012, largely to converse with the “erudite and knowledgeable politician that he always remained”.
Hitting back at Ms. Gandhi, Sharmistha Mukherjee, the late President’s daughter, said it was not a crime to be ambitious.
“What’s there to be shocked about?” she asked in a post on X in response to Ms. Gandhi’s remarks.

“Is it a crime to be ambitious, especially when that ‘ambition’ was supported by decades of experience in politics and governance, hard work and a brilliant mind? Once, when asked by me whether he wanted to become PM, he very candidly answered that ‘any politician worth his salt has this ambition’,” she wrote.

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes

In her memoir, former Congress president recalls 2010 conversation; Pranab Mukherjee’s daughter Sharmistha asks what there was to be shocked about, says it is not a crime to be ambitious

Former President Pranab Mukherjee had “shocked” Sonia Gandhi by hinting at his “long-held desire” to become Prime Minister during a conversation with her in 2010, suggesting that perhaps it was time for a “change at the top”, the former Congress president has written in her memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love .

The book, published by HarperCollins, was made available in bookstores on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), but the official launch is likely to take place on November 16.

Mukherjee, then a senior member of the Manmohan Singh Cabinet, had developed serious differences with the then Finance Minister P. Chidambaram. He would sometimes stay back for conversations with Ms. Gandhi after meetings of the Congress Strategy Group, which was set up to discuss parliamentary business.

“On one occasion, in 2010, I think after expressing his frustration, he shocked me with the suggestion that perhaps it was time for a change at the top, which I understood as a hint of his long-held desire to become Prime Minister,” she wrote.

“I gently changed the subject, and though he may have been disappointed, he never made me feel he held it against me,” she added.

The late Mukherjee, who had served in Indira Gandhi’s Cabinet in the 1970s, was part of a core group that met weekly with Dr. Singh to coordinate the functioning of the government and the party. Other members included Arjun Singh, A.K. Antony and Ahmed Patel.

Ms. Gandhi says she often called on Mukherjee after he became President in 2012, largely to converse with the “erudite and knowledgeable politician that he always remained”.

Hitting back at Ms. Gandhi, Sharmistha Mukherjee, the late President’s daughter, said it was not a crime to be ambitious.

“What’s there to be shocked about?” she asked in a post on X in response to Ms. Gandhi’s remarks.

“Is it a crime to be ambitious, especially when that ‘ambition’ was supported by decades of experience in politics and governance, hard work and a brilliant mind? Once, when asked by me whether he wanted to become PM, he very candidly answered that ‘any politician worth his salt has this ambition’,” she wrote.

articles.title: After Bangladesh rules out passport for Hasina, India says ‘travel document’ needed
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal described the passport’s requirement for extradition as a “technical issue” and said, “Obviously, for the travel of people, you need a travel document”

A day after the Acting Foreign Minister of Bangladesh, Humayun Kabir, stressed that Dhaka would not issue a passport to deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and insisted on getting her extradited from India under an “acceptable prisoner exchange”, the Ministry of External Affairs said on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) that a “travel document” was needed for international travel.

“Extradition of former Prime Minister of Bangladesh Sheikh Hasina is a legal matter and it will be dealt with accordingly,” said Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal in response to a question about Ms. Hasina’s presence in India. He described the passport’s requirement for extradition as a “technical issue” and said, “Obviously, for the travel of people, you need a travel document.”
Officials said Ms. Hasina can be extradited either on a Bangladeshi passport or an Emergency Certificate that would prove that she has Bangladeshi citizenship.

On Monday (November 9, 2026), Mr. Kabir cited the extradition treaty between India and Bangladesh, which was signed during the Hasina era in 2013, and said, “Bangladesh will not issue a passport to any terrorist; there is no provision for such an action. Bangladesh will seek the return of Sheikh Hasina through an acceptable prisoner exchange process.”

An official dealing with the matter told The Hindu on Monday (November 9, 2026) that a passport was required for extradition. The deposed Prime Minister has sought a new passport and a national identity document through a London-based law firm that has written to the Bangladesh government.

Bangladesh has a history of leaders going into exile or being imprisoned for long periods after returning. Current Prime Minister Tarique Rahman was in exile for nearly 17 years before he returned from the United Kingdom on December 25, 2025.
On August 5, 2026, Ms. Hasina had announced at a virtual press conference that she would return to Bangladesh in December this year.

Over the past few days, the law and order situation has deteriorated across Bangladesh, with incidents of violence, looting, and arson being reported. On Tuesday (November 10, 2026), Jamaat-e-Islami and the National Citizen Party, which are in the Opposition, accused the government of failing to maintain law and order.

Leader of the Opposition, Shafiqur Rahman, said the country’s Home Ministry has failed to contain the situation. “Even the Army Golf Club has now witnessed cocktail explosions. Similar incidents have occurred in front of the Special Branch headquarters, at police station gates, and at Dhaka University, where explosions have taken place for three consecutive days. Two people were injured there,” he said.

articles.title: Bihar CM suspends 15 officers for negligence of duty
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Nine officers of Revenue and Land Reforms Department (RLRD) four officers from the Public Health Engineering Department and one officer each from the Rural Development Department and the Urban Development Department have faced the action.

Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) suspended 15 officers with immediate effect for negligence and failure to ensure the quality resolution of applications under the ‘Sahyog’ (Assistance) Programme.
The action has been taken and departmental proceedings have also been initiated against them for failing to process applications in a timely manner,

Nine officers of Revenue and Land Reforms Department (RLRD), four officers from the Public Health Engineering Department and one officer each from the Rural Development Department and the Urban Development Department have faced the action.
The officers include Block Development Officers (BDOs) and Circle Officers (COs), assistance engineers and junior engineers.

“All officers and personnel must extend their full cooperation in the processing of applications. It is our duty to address everyone’s problems with sensitivity and promptness, and to ensure they receive justice,” Mr. Choudhary said while holding the ‘State-Level Sahyog Programme at Chief Minister’s Secretariat where 76 applications were received.

He further said that the government’s objective is to ensure a transparent, fair, and time-bound resolution to every citizen’s grievance. The ‘Sahyog’ camps are intended to address public concerns and ensure citizen satisfaction.

Mr. Choudhary has directed all District Magistrates, departmental secretaries, and officials within the Chief Minister’s Secretariat to go beyond merely reviewing the timeliness of the resolution of applications received through the ‘Sahyog’ portal; they must also conduct a thorough review of the quality of these resolutions.

The initiative, which was launched for the first time by Mr. Choudhary, is part of the state government’s ‘Ease of Living’ under the ambitious ‘Saat Nischay-3’ programme aimed at delivering services at citizens’ doorsteps.

At the time of launching the initiative in May 19, 2026, it was already mentioned that if a case is not resolved within 30 days of receiving the application, suspension and disciplinary action will be taken against the responsible officers. These camps are organised on the first and third Tuesdays of every month to address complaints related to block offices, police stations, and revenue offices.
Mr. Choudhary instructed officials to ensure that the grievances of the general public are addressed with complete clarity and transparency.

articles.title: Producers welcome proposal for minimum sustainable price for tea
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tea Board of India has recommended a proposal to the Ministry of Commerce to implement minimum sustainable price (MSP) for tea. Several stake holders said that MSP is essential for long-term sustainability of the industry

Observing that a committee of Tea Board of India has recommended a proposal to implement minimum sustainable price for tea, several stakeholders of the tea industry on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) welcomed the proposal and said that such an initiative will help in increasing wages of tea garden workers and is essential for long term sustainability of the industry.

Representatives of different associations associated with the industry expressed apprehensions that with implementation of the Code on Wages, there will be a further increase in wage costs, and the financial viability of tea producers is likely to face additional challenges

“The tea industry is confronted with mounting cost pressures, while tea price realisations have remained relatively stagnant. A Minimum Sustainable Price framework is therefore essential to bridge the widening gap between production costs and market realisations and to ensure the long-term sustainability of the industry,” said C. K Dhanuka, Chairman, Dhunseri Tea and Industries. Mr. Dhanuka added that a minimum sustainable price will help bring realisations in line with costs, so that the industry can accommodate wage revisions, protect employment and the competitiveness of Indian tea.
The proposal of implementing minimum sustainable price for tea have been made to Ministry of Commerce, which is yet to take a decision on the proposal, the stakeholders of tea industry said.

Suneel Singh Sikand, chairman of Indian Tea Association (ITA) called the recommendation for a minimum sustainable price is an important policy intervention towards addressing the structural challenges confronting the Indian tea industry.

“Ensuring remunerative returns to producers is critical to sustaining operations, facilitating investment in re-plantation and productivity enhancement and securing the industry’s long-term sustainability,” Mr. Sikand said.

Hemanta Bangur, former president of ITA said that the industry has failed to uplift the workforce and something is fundamentally wrong with the industry as the balance sheet of most of the tea growers is in the red.
“The market is dysfunctional and there is no level playing field. If market forces are left to determine the fate of industry, it will bring about the demise of tea gardens,” he said.
The Tea Industry employs millions of workers in about 270 large tea gardens and hundreds of small tea gardens across the State. The daily wage for a tea garden worker in West Bengal is ₹250 per day.

Representatives of Indian Tea Association (ITA), Tea Association of India (TAI), United Planters’ Association of Southern India (UPASI), Confederation of Indian Small Tea Growers Associations (CISTA) and Federation of Indian Tea Manufacturers Association (FITMA) issued a press statement on the stagnation in the prices over the past several years

articles.title: Bombay High Court declines request for hearing each day in quota petitions for Maratha reservation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Bombay High Court on November 5 declined a request to hear each day a set of petitions on a quota of 10% for Marathas in education and service under the State. The court said hearing will continue on November 27. The document in the case is PIL 30 of 2024, Bhausaheb Bhujangrao Pawar vs State of Maharashtra.

A Bench of Justices Makarand Karnik, Nijamoodin Jamadar and Sandeep Marne passed the order. The Bench said it considered the request. It said efforts were being made to give priority to the PIL and matters that relate to it. It said a session for hearing was being assigned at intervals after taking into account work load from assignments. It said the matters were being heard at intervals. It said it would not accede to the request.

The Bench was constituted in September and has heard the matter four times since September 18, 2026. It has heard submissions from advocate Arvind Datar for a petitioner who challenges the quota. It is hearing petitioners.

The legislature passed the Act on February 20, 2024, and it was subsequently notified on February 26, 2024. The Act rests on a report of the commission under Justice Sunil Shukre. The report cited circumstances and situations as reason to grant reservation to Marathas beyond the 50% limit.

A petitioner moved the Bombay High Court against the SEBC Act, 2018, enacted by the government under Devendra Fadnavis. That law gave Marathas 16% reservation in employment under the State and in education. The High Court upheld the law in June 2019. It held that justification did not exist for the 16% quota and reduced it to 12% in education and 13% in employment under the State. Patil and others challenged that verdict in the Supreme Court. In May 2021, a Bench of the Supreme Court struck down the SEBC Act, 2018. It held that no circumstances justified reservation for Marathas beyond the 50% ceiling set by the 1992 Indra Sawhney judgment. The Supreme Court also questioned the data in support of backwardness of Marathas. The government filed a review petition. The Supreme Court rejected it in April 2023. A petition for relief after review is before the Supreme Court.

fullParagraphs: The 137-page report, released by the GOP-controlled committee, comes nearly a year after Congress passed and President Trump signed the Epstein Files Transparency Act

The Republican-led House Oversight Committee slammed the Trump administration on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) for botching the public release of millions of pages of records relating to disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein.

In a report scrutinising the government’s handling of criminal investigations of Epstein and his longtime confidant Ghislaine Maxwell, the committee faulted President Donald Trump and the Justice Department for reneging on a promise to open the files, which led Congress to pass a law forcing their release.

After Congress stepped in, the administration missed disclosure deadlines and concealed names of alleged co-conspirators while failing to adequately protect victims, “including through deficient redactions that exposed their sensitive information,” the report said.

The 137-page report, released by the GOP-controlled committee, comes nearly a year after Congress passed and Mr. Trump signed the Epstein Files Transparency Act, which requires the Justice Department to publicly disclose records relating to the late sex offender, many of which were previously confidential. The report also comes on the heels of last week’s midterm elections, when Republicans suffered heavy House losses in failing to hold their majority after a campaign where the release of government records related to Epstein became a recurring campaign issue.

“The Trump administration has repeatedly committed to releasing Epstein-related files,” the report said. “However, multiple shortcomings related to releasing documents and failures to adequately communicate about those releases plagued the DOJ’s efforts.”

Democrats used the Trump administration’s handling of the files to accuse Republicans of protecting the wealthy and well-connected, suggesting Trump’s past relationship with Epstein exposed him to potential unethical activity. The report stated, “Trump’s lack of involvement is confirmed by numerous lines of testimony in interviews or depositions with various individuals.”

The Justice Department released the bulk of the so-called Epstein files in December and January. In all, more than 3 million pages of documents were disclosed, along with more than 2,000 videos and 180,000 images. Then-Attorney General Pam Bondi’s handling of the Epstein files contributed to her firing in April.

The records included documents concerning Epstein’s famous associates, including Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, formerly known as Britain’s Prince Andrew, and email correspondence between Epstein and Elon Musk and other prominent contacts from across the political spectrum.

More than 350 different ads mentioning Epstein aired since Labour Day for Republican and Democratic candidates running in the Nov. 3 midterm elections, according to the ad-tracking firm AdImpact. articles.title: U.S. Republicans derail bid to impeach Hegseth
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The House voted 211 to 204 to send the impeachment resolution to the Judiciary Committee; this halts the immediate impeachment drive but does not prevent Democrats from reviving the effort after taking control of Congress in January

Republicans in the U.S. House of Representatives on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) blocked an effort to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth over the Iran war , handing President Donald Trump a victory days after his party's crushing midterm election defeat.

The House voted 211 to 204 to send the impeachment resolution to the Judiciary Committee, effectively derailing a planned vote on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) on whether to bring formal charges against the embattled Pentagon chief.
The resolution was introduced by Republican Thomas Massie, a Trump critic who was the only member of his party to oppose the procedural maneuver, according to U.S. media.
ALSO WATCH What are the impeachment charges against Pete Hegseth? | The Hindu Explains

The impeachment drive had threatened to deepen Mr. Trump's troubles after Democrats swept last week's midterms, with anger at the sputtering Iran war and soaring fuel prices helping drive voters to a historic rejection of Republicans.
Republicans still hold a narrow House majority until January, when Democrats take control of both chambers of Congress. And 11 Democrats missed the vote.
Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell, in a post on X, hailed the vote as a "TOTAL VICTORY!"
"We look forward to ending this sham impeachment in the committee room, where facts will continue to prevail and this distraction can be put to rest."
Mr. Hegseth earlier on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) dismissed the impeachment effort as a "farce" and defended his record leading the Iran war and other military operations under Mr. Trump.
"It's a farce, and it's a stunt, and everybody knows it," he said at a Pentagon press conference, branding the accusations "slander" and "sabotage."

articles.title: Trump ally Jim Jordan elected U.S. House Republican leader after midterm election rout
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Ohio Congressman will replace House Speaker Mike Johnson, who announced he was stepping down from leadership after Republicans lost control of both chambers of Congress

Jim Jordan, a hardline ally of President Donald Trump, was elected leader of the Republicans in the U.S. House of Representatives on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), defeating fellow conservative Steve Scalise as the party reckons with a crushing midterm election defeat.

Mr. Jordan, the combative chairman of the House Judiciary Committee, beat the current majority leader by 106 votes to 73 in a secret ballot, U.S. media reported, putting him in charge of the party's opposition to the incoming Democratic majority.
The Ohio congressman will replace House Speaker Mike Johnson, who announced he was stepping down from leadership after Republicans lost control of both chambers of Congress in last week's elections.
Senate Republicans meanwhile reelected John Thune as their leader, retaining their existing leadership team despite demands from conservatives for a reckoning over the election losses.
Mr. Jordan, a founding member of the hard-right House Freedom Caucus, had pitched himself as the fighter Republicans need to confront Democrats during the final two years of Trump's presidency.
His victory represented a rejection of the party's established leadership, with Mr. Scalise having served in senior Republican positions for more than a decade.
Both men are staunch Trump allies, but the president declined to endorse either candidate.
The contest was a rematch of their 2023 battle for the speakership following the ouster of Kevin McCarthy.

Mr. Scalise initially won the Republican nomination but withdrew after failing to secure sufficient support, while Mr. Jordan subsequently lost three votes on the House floor before Mr. Johnson emerged as a compromise candidate.

Mr. Jordan, a former champion wrestler who has represented Ohio in Congress since 2007, built his reputation as a political brawler and fierce critic of the Republican establishment. Former speaker John Boehner once branded him a "legislative terrorist" for his uncompromising tactics.

The Ohio Congressman will replace House Speaker Mike Johnson, who announced he was stepping down from leadership after Republicans lost control of both chambers of Congress

Jim Jordan, a hardline ally of President Donald Trump, was elected leader of the Republicans in the U.S. House of Representatives on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), defeating fellow conservative Steve Scalise as the party reckons with a crushing midterm election defeat.

Mr. Jordan, the combative chairman of the House Judiciary Committee, beat the current majority leader by 106 votes to 73 in a secret ballot, U.S. media reported, putting him in charge of the party's opposition to the incoming Democratic majority.

The Ohio congressman will replace House Speaker Mike Johnson, who announced he was stepping down from leadership after Republicans lost control of both chambers of Congress in last week's elections.

Senate Republicans meanwhile reelected John Thune as their leader, retaining their existing leadership team despite demands from conservatives for a reckoning over the election losses.

Mr. Jordan, a founding member of the hard-right House Freedom Caucus, had pitched himself as the fighter Republicans need to confront Democrats during the final two years of Trump's presidency.

His victory represented a rejection of the party's established leadership, with Mr. Scalise having served in senior Republican positions for more than a decade.

Both men are staunch Trump allies, but the president declined to endorse either candidate.

The contest was a rematch of their 2023 battle for the speakership following the ouster of Kevin McCarthy.

Mr. Scalise initially won the Republican nomination but withdrew after failing to secure sufficient support, while Mr. Jordan subsequently lost three votes on the House floor before Mr. Johnson emerged as a compromise candidate.

Mr. Jordan, a former champion wrestler who has represented Ohio in Congress since 2007, built his reputation as a political brawler and fierce critic of the Republican establishment. Former speaker John Boehner once branded him a "legislative terrorist" for his uncompromising tactics.

articles.title: U.S. Senate Republicans vote to keep John Thune as leader after steep midterm election losses
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: South Dakota Sen. John Thune has spent much of the last two years navigating President Trump, who has often been at odds with the Senate

U.S. Senate Republicans reelected South Dakota Sen. John Thune as their leader on Tuesday (November 11, 2026) after a tense day of private discussions about steep losses in the midterm elections that cost them their majority.

Mr. Thune was always expected to prevail, as he is popular with his GOP colleagues and was running unopposed in the secret-ballot election. But Senate Republicans vented their frustrations in three separate meetings on Tuesday (November 11, 2026) after an election wipeout that cost them at least seven Senate seats.

Some Republicans had tried to delay the leadership decision, but the conference voted 31-15 to proceed. Wisconsin Sen. Ron Johnson led the effort to postpone and walked out when it failed. The closed-door meetings were held in the small Old Senate Chamber with few aides in attendance.
As the conference debated earlier in the day, West Virginia Sen. Jim Justice said “we want to be thoughtful and do the right thing.”
He said there was a “legitimate argument that, good gracious, if we lost as badly as we lost, why would we continue on with the same leadership?”
At the same time, the current GOP leadership “didn't cause this problem to happen,” Justice said. “They do a good job.”

Republicans' angst and indecision come as frustrated Republicans are just beginning to reckon with what the election results mean for their future — and for their relationship with President Donald Trump, as voters resoundingly rejected their two years of single-party rule in Congress and the White House. Two additional Senate races remain uncalled in Alaska and Mississippi that could further deplete their numbers.

“I just think that we've got a lot of things that we've got to think through, and I think that to just rush into this and just ratify all of the same leadership, what message does that send?” Missouri Sen. Josh Hawley told reporters after the first meeting.

“If you don't think after losing seven Senate seats minimum that we need to change course, I don't know what planet you're on,” said Mr. Hawley, who voted to delay the elections. He said he wasn't aware of anyone else running for leader, but “maybe there would be” if they waited.

Others said Mr. Thune wasn't the problem. “I don't think it was the fault of our leadership, quite frankly," said West Virginia Sen. Shelley Moore Capito, who was reelected to her leadership position as GOP policy chair.

articles.title: Canada has not made a decision about lifting Arctic drilling ban, says Mark Carney
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Toronto Star reported that Mr. Carney’s government is considering lifting the ban on oil and gas activities in the Arctic, quoting a Department of Finance official

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said on ​Tuesday (November 10, 2026) that his government has not made a decision about lifting its ⁠decade-long moratorium on offshore oil and gas exploration in the Arctic, a move that some Northern leaders have advocated for as a way to increase the region’s economic self-sufficiency.

Last week’s federal budget contained a reference ‌to C$11 million ($7.79 million) in funding over four years to “support the governance and oversight of offshore oil and gas activities in the Arctic Ocean.” Mr. Carney told reporters ‌in Montreal the budget item represents “capacity funding” for Inuit leadership, with whom the federal government ‌has ⁠agreed to jointly manage natural resources in the North.
“It is absolutely not, in ⁠any way, shape or form, a decision about lifting the moratorium,” Mr. Carney said. “It is respectful engagement with that self-government.”

“Any possible discussion with respect to the future of the moratorium would respect existing agreements, Inuit and territorial self-government, and uphold ​Canada’s strong environmental standards,” Canada’s Minister of ‌Northern and Arctic Affairs Rebecca Chartrand said in an emailed statement.

Mr. Carney has been seeking to grow Canada’s energy sector in order to boost the country’s economy in the face of U.S. tariffs. He has faced criticism from environmentalists for the dropping or easing of a ‌range of climate regulations in pursuit of economic growth.

The Toronto Star reported on ​Monday (November 9, 2026) that Mr. Carney’s government is considering lifting the ban on oil and gas activities in the Arctic, quoting a Department of Finance official. The Finance Department ⁠referred Reuters to Crown-Indigenous Relations and Northern Affairs Canada, which did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Canada’s moratorium on Arctic offshore oil and gas exploration has been in place since 2016, ‌when then-Prime Minister Justin Trudeau and then-U.S. President Barack Obama agreed to impose it to protect the region’s fragile marine ecosystem from the risk of oil spills.

U.S. President Donald Trump later reopened parts of the Arctic to oil and gas drilling, but the Canadian moratorium remained in place. The Canadian policy, which is set to expire in 2028, is reviewed every five years.
Canada’s Arctic region possesses significant undeveloped oil and gas reserves, and some Northern leaders have been ‌calling for the area to be opened up to drilling.

Nunavut Premier John Main told the National Observer media outlet ​last week he wants to see the territory’s fossil fuel industry take off, so that Canada’s north can become more economically self-sufficient.

articles.title: Firecrackers still Delhi’s top pollutant after Deepavali, IITM finds
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The contribution of firecrackers to the city's pollution levels was significantly higher on November 9, a day after Deepavali, before declining on November 11, the IITM models showed

Firecrackers emerged as the biggest contributor to Delhi's air pollution on both Monday (November 9, 2026) and Tuesday (November 10), accounting for 71.1% and 29.8% of the pollution load, respectively, according to source-apportionment estimates by the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM).

The contribution of firecrackers to the city's pollution levels was significantly higher on Monday (November 9), a day after Deepavali, before declining on Tuesday (November 11), the IITM models showed.

The estimates had a standard deviation (SD) of 104.1 percentage points on Monday (November 9) and 27.7 percentage points on Tuesday (November 10), indicating considerable variability and uncertainty in the modelled contributions.

On Monday (November 9), vehicular emissions accounted for 6.9% of the pollution, followed by secondary inorganic aerosols at 5% and secondary organic aerosols at 4.5%. Mixed or unresolved biofuel contributed 4.45%, while mineral dust and ash and mixed combustion accounted for 2.5% each.

Wood burning contributed 1.3%, while waste burning, including municipal and plastic-rubber-containing waste, accounted for 1.1%. Coal combustion and industrial emissions contributed 0.5% and 0.2%, respectively.
On Tuesday (November 10), the contribution of firecrackers dropped to 29.8%, while secondary organic aerosols emerged as the second-largest contributor at 17.5%.
Vehicular emissions and secondary inorganic aerosols each accounted for 11.7% of the pollution load, while wood burning contributed 10.7% and waste burning 7.7%.
Vehicular emissions emerged as the third largest contributor to pollution on Tuesday (November 10).
Mixed combustion accounted for 5.1%, followed by mixed or unresolved biofuel at 3.3% and mineral dust and ash at 1.5%.
Delhi's average 24-hour Air Quality Index (AQI) had improved marginally to the 'poor' category on Tuesday (November 10), with the 4 p.m. reading settling at 299.

articles.title: Over eight lakh glass bangles adorn Goddess Kanaka Durga for ‘Gajula Alankaram’ in Vijayawada
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The temple doubles the number of bangles used last year to decorate the deity and its premises

Indrakeeladri, the abode of Goddess Kanaka Durga in Vijayawada , came alive with ‘Gajula Alankaram’ (bangle decoration) of Goddess Kanaka Durga on Wednesday (November 11, 2026), on the auspicious occasion of ‘Kartika Shuddha Vidiya’ , observed as ‘Bhagini Hasta Bhojanam’ .

Over eight lakh colourful glass bangles were used to adorn the presiding deity and decorate the premises of the Sri Durga Malleswara Swamy Varla Devasthanam, including the sanctum sanctorum, corridors, ceilings and sub-shrines. The bangles, in vibrant shades of green, red, yellow and blue, were intricately arranged into garlands and decorative patterns.

Goddess Kanaka Durga adorned with glass bangles for Gajula Alankaram on Indrakeeladri in Vijayawada on Wednesday. Over eight lakh bangles decorated the deity and the temple, double last year's number. Photos: K.V.S. Giri https://t.co/rv91oEsxb0

Temple Executive Officer V.K. Seena Naik said all arrangements had been completed in accordance with temple traditions and customs. Inspecting the arrangements on the sixth floor of the Maha Mantapam, he said the temple had used over four lakh bangles last year, while their number had been doubled this year to decorate both the main deity and the temple premises.
He said devotees and donors had contributed bangles in large quantities, with the temple administration making additional arrangements to meet the requirement.

Women devotees from different parts of the State thronged the temple to have darshan of the Goddess in the special alankaram. Following the rituals, the bangles worshipped in the presence of the deity were distributed to women devotees as prasadam.

Women devotees from different parts of the State thronged the temple to have darshan of the Goddess in the special ‘alankaram’ . Following the rituals, the bangles worshipped in the presence of the deity were distributed to women devotees as ‘prasadam’ .
Temple officials monitored queue management, drinking water supply and prasadam distribution to facilitate the smooth movement of devotees.

articles.title: The controversy surrounding procuring books for the Periyar Arivulagam | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The controversy caused a furore in Tamil Nadu, as the case heads into a Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption inquiry, court intervention and the scope of investigations has now explanded to include inventories in several other libraries

The story so far: A veritable pandora’s box of literary and political controversy was opened on November 6, 2026, when Sahitya Akademi winner Perumal Murugan wrote about several irregularities in the procurement of books for the newly-inaugurated Periyar Arivulagam library in Coimbatore. He wrote, and later spoke online, about how thousands of exorbitantly-priced books had been procured for the library with questionable authorship, full of factual errors and were seemingly AI generated. He also pointed out that these books had been procured at inflated rates, many times higher than current market rates for similar publications.

It has since caused a furore in Tamil Nadu, as the case heads into a Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption inquiry, court intervention and the scope of investigations has now explanded to include inventories in several other libraries, and it has also started an intense political blame game with the prime actors being the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) and its predecessor, now in the Opposition, the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam.

articles.title: Mafia rule prevails at every level in Bihar, claims RJD's Tejashwi Yadav
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Targeting Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, the RJD national working president asserted that his lack of administrative acumen, inexperience and ineffective leadership had left the police and bureaucracy virtually unaccountable

RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) accused the NDA government in Bihar of “allowing the mafia to establish its influence”, while alleging that the state had descended into “financial disorder and administrative mismanagement”.

In a post on X, Mr. Yadav, who is also the Leader of Opposition in the State assembly, claimed that corruption, deteriorating law and order and poor governance had become deep-rooted structural problems under the present regime, affecting every section of society and all institutions.

बिहार वित्तीय अराजकता, प्रशासनिक कुव्यवस्था, बदइंतज़ामी, अनुशासनहीनता और राजशून्यता का पर्याय बन चुका है। कुशासन, बदहाल विधि व्यवस्था और भ्रष्टाचार एनडीए सरकार में गहरी व गंभीर संरचनात्मक समस्या बन चुका है जो सरकार और समाज के हर स्तर पर प्रत्येक व्यक्ति एवं व्यवस्था को प्रभावित कर रहा है। हर स्तर पर माफिया का राज है। इससे दुर्भाग्यपूर्ण क्या होगा कि अपराधी पुलिस की हत्या कर रहे है और पुलिस अपनी ख़ामियाँ छुपाने के लिए निर्दोष नागरिकों की हत्या कर रही है। आपराधिक प्रवृत्ति के अनाड़ी मुख्यमंत्री से बिहार संभल नहीं रहा है जिससे बिहार में अराजक और विध्वंसक स्थिति उत्पन्न हो चुकी है। बिहार में गवर्नेंस नाम की कोई चीज़ ही नहीं है। मनोनीत मुख्यमंत्री के अल्पज्ञान, अनाड़ी कार्यशैली एवं अकुशलता के कारण अधिकारी इन्हें गंभीरता से नहीं ले रहे है। जनसमस्याओं का निदान, जनसरोकर और जनजीवन को बेहतर बनाना मुख्यमंत्री की प्राथमिकता ही नहीं है और यही वजह है कि नावाकिफ अपरिपक्व मुख्यमंत्री लोक कल्याणकारी मुद्दों की बजाय ग़ैर वाजिब मुद्दों को तरजीह देते रहते है। नौकरी-रोजगार, गुणवत्तापूर्ण शिक्षा, बेहतर स्वास्थ्य व विधि व्यवस्था, औद्योगिक तथा इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर विस्तार, टेक्नोलॉजी, विकास एवं निवेश तो मुख्यमंत्री के शब्दकोश में ही नहीं है। मुख्यमंत्री के नौसखियापन, नासमझी और कम-अक़्ली के कारण पुलिस और प्रशासन बेलगाम है। भ्रष्टाचार सारी सीमाएँ तोड़ चुका है। वोट चोरी से सत्ता में आए सत्यापित ठगों ने क्या बिहार को बर्बादी के गर्त में धकेलने के लिए मनोनीत मुख्यमंत्री के हाथों में बागडोर सौंपी है?
"Mafia rule prevails at every level. What could be more unfortunate than criminals killing policemen, while police personnel are killing innocent citizens to cover up their own lapses?" he alleged.

Targeting Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, the RJD national working president asserted that his “lack of administrative acumen, inexperience and ineffective leadership had left the police and bureaucracy virtually unaccountable”.

Mr. Yadav also claimed that senior officials were not taking the CM seriously and public welfare, employment, quality education, healthcare, law and order and improving people's lives were “missing from his priorities”.
Industrial growth, infrastructure development, technology, investment and employment generation have taken a back seat in the state under the NDA government, he alleged.

Claiming that corruption has crossed all limits and governance has virtually collapsed, Mr. Yadav wondered whether the NDA handed over the state's reins to a "nominated chief minister" to push Bihar “towards ruin”, while accusing those in power of securing office “through vote theft”.

articles.title: Passengers on Bengaluru-Mangaluru-Goa VB Express pay nearly ₹200 extra fare compared to same distance on other VB services
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Charging fares inflating the distance by 40% on Konkan Railway network between Thokur and Madgaon and 100% on 55 km Sakleshpur-Subrahmanya Road Ghat section the reason for extra fares

Patrons travelling the Yeshwantpur-Madgaon-Yeshwantpur Vande Bharat Express (Train No. 26655/656) from November 15 will pay nearly ₹200 extra fare in chair car (CC) and about ₹300 extra on executive chair car (EC) when compared to the same distance travelled on other Vande Bharat services.

The actual base fare, for example, between Yeshwantpur and Madgaon in CC would be around ₹1,186 and in EC, around ₹2,444. However, the actual distance of 670 km gets inflated to around 844 km increasing the base fare to ₹1,369 in CC (₹183 extra) and ₹2,795 (₹351 extra) in EC classes. The base fare excludes reservation charges of ₹40 and ₹60, superfast charges of ₹45 and ₹75, respectively, for these classes and 5% GST on all these charges. If the passenger opts for onboard food, catering charges ranging from ₹300 to ₹600, would be extra.

For Karwar, the likely base fare could be ₹1,292 as against the actual ₹1,100 in CC (₹192 extra) and ₹2,642 as against ₹2,253 in EC class; for Udupi, it could be ₹931 as against ₹809 (₹122 extra) in CC and ₹1,890 as against ₹1,651 (₹239 extra) in EC and for Mangaluru Junction, the base fare could be ₹809 as against the actual ₹721 (₹88 extra) in CC and ₹1,561 as against the actual ₹1,468 (₹93 extra) in EC class.
Source: Railway Ministry’s fare chart for premium services

Normal fares are collected on other VB expresses operating in Karnataka for almost similar distances. For example, the base fares on Mangaluru-Thiruvananthapuram Central VB Express have been ₹1,131 and ₹2,295 for CC and EC respectively for 620 km distance; KSR Bengaluru-Ernakulam Junction VB Express at ₹1,159 and ₹2,352 for 625 km; KSR Bengaluru-Belagavi VB Express at ₹1,132 and ₹2,295 for 612 km and on Yeshwantpur-Kacheguda VB, the base fares have been ₹1,113 and ₹2,267 for CC and EC respectively.
A 16-car Brand new Vande Bharat rake is kept ready for the November 15 inaugural run of Madgaon-Yeshwantpur VB Express from Mangaluru Junction on November 11, 2026. | Photo Credit: H S MANJUNATH

The extra fare becomes applicable as the Konkan Railway Corporation Ltd., (KRCL) on whose network half of the route passes through, inflates the distance by 40% to calculate passenger fares and by 50% for freight charges. KRCL network begins from Thokur near Mangaluru and extends till Roha in Maharashtra surpassing Madgaon. Thus, about 300 km distance between Thokur and Madgaon gets inflated to 416 km.

At the same time, the South Western Railway (SWR) inflates the 55 km distance on the Ghat section between Sakleshpur and Subrahmanya Road by 100%, making the chargeable distance to 110 km. Thus, the end-to-end inflated chargeable distance becomes about 844 km against the actual 670 km distance.

The SWR justified the inflated distance saying the Indian Railways follows the practice on almost all Ghat routes because of the challenges in operating through difficult terrains. KRCL was initially allowed to inflate the distance to recover the construction cost of about ₹3,555 crore. The Corporation now justifies the additional collection due to “heavy maintenance cost (due to difficult geographical conditions).”

She was building a career in Chinese finance before turning to tech with a leadership role at a data centre company in Singapore. He is the high-profile CEO of Nvidia, the California-based company that makes computer chips relied upon by advanced artificial intelligence systems.
An affair between Nvidia's Jensen Huang and Alice Huang, who reportedly was suspected of working as a spy for Beijing, has rocked the tech and political worlds.
The Chinese businesswoman also known as Huang Le had a close relationship with Jensen Huang, according to reports over the past month by the New York Times.

The newspaper also reported that top policymakers were informed in a memo that intelligence indicated she was a spy for China's Ministry of State Security, recruited to influence Nvidia to make its most advanced chips more available in China.

In one widely shared photograph of the pair, Jensen Huang and people surrounding him are holding drinks in Taipei, while Alice Huang sits behind him, apparently watching him in conversation. The picture was posted in 2024 by software company NetThunder to its LinkedIn page.
It remains unclear how long the affair lasted, and when exactly the relationship might have ended. The Associated Press was unable to reach Alice Huang for comment.
Publicly available information about Alice Huang is scant.
She was a Chinese finance executive before becoming involved in artificial intelligence, data centres and computer chips.

In 2023, she became a director at Singapore-based Megaspeed, which describes itself as an “NVIDIA cloud partner”. Last year, Megaspeed faced scrutiny from the U.S. over its alleged skirting of U.S. export restrictions and routing of a large amount of advanced Nvidia chips for Chinese users.

Megaspeed was incorporated in 2015 in Singapore with the name 7Road International, after being spun off as the overseas arm of a Chinese video game developer, according to corporate registration records.

articles.title: Spain’s first general strike in 14 years brings clashing social and political desires to the fore
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The two main unions calling for the strike, UGT and CCOO, reported widespread participation in the early hours “with significant work stoppages in strategic sectors”

Millions of Spain’s workers are striking on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) to demand that the government remedy the nation’s housing crisis less than three weeks before a national election that could catapult the far right to power.

Spain’s first general strike in 14 years is expected to cause delays to the widely used public transport system and lead to the slowdown or shuttering of businesses, factories and shops across the eurozone’s fourth largest economy.

Minor incidents were reported in the first hours, including roadblocks — some of them with burning tyres — in Barcelona, the second-largest city in the country, and scuffles between picketers and police near the country’s main wholesale market on the outskirts of the capital, Madrid. Striking workers set off fireworks on the stroke of midnight as they gathered in public squares in Barcelona.

The two main unions calling for the strike, UGT and CCOO, reported widespread participation in the early hours “with significant work stoppages in strategic sectors” — 90% in the automotive and port sectors, 85% in the meat industry, 82% in waste collection, and 75% in the energy sector — according to a statement posted on social media.
Between workers, activists, politicians and ordinary Spaniards, the groups have very different interests in Wednesday's (November 11) walkout.
The average rent in Spain has almost doubled in the last 10 years, eating into household budgets and angering voters.

Public anger over housing reached a boiling point following the nationally televised eviction of an 87-year-old woman from her home in Madrid last month. The subsequent death of Maricarmen, as the woman became known, caused even more indignation and solidified her as a symbol of Spaniards who feel they pay too much on rent and can’t even dream of homeownership.
Housing activists leveraged the uproar over Maricarmen's eviction to call for the general strike. They soon won the backing of Spain's two main unions, UGT and CCOO.

The housing activists want several measures, including the elimination of tourist apartments, a crackdown on real estate speculation and protection for renters in the form of automatic renewals of leases.
The UGT and CCOO unions are demanding more government intervention in the housing market and a new minimum wage agreement through talks with the business owners' association.

🎯 Exam Relevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy

The two main unions calling for the strike, UGT and CCOO, reported widespread participation in the early hours “with significant work stoppages in strategic sectors”

Millions of Spain’s workers are striking on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) to demand that the government remedy the nation’s housing crisis less than three weeks before a national election that could catapult the far right to power.

Spain’s first general strike in 14 years is expected to cause delays to the widely used public transport system and lead to the slowdown or shuttering of businesses, factories and shops across the eurozone’s fourth largest economy.

Minor incidents were reported in the first hours, including roadblocks — some of them with burning tyres — in Barcelona, the second-largest city in the country, and scuffles between picketers and police near the country’s main wholesale market on the outskirts of the capital, Madrid. Striking workers set off fireworks on the stroke of midnight as they gathered in public squares in Barcelona.

The two main unions calling for the strike, UGT and CCOO, reported widespread participation in the early hours “with significant work stoppages in strategic sectors” — 90% in the automotive and port sectors, 85% in the meat industry, 82% in waste collection, and 75% in the energy sector — according to a statement posted on social media.

Between workers, activists, politicians and ordinary Spaniards, the groups have very different interests in Wednesday's (November 11) walkout.

The average rent in Spain has almost doubled in the last 10 years, eating into household budgets and angering voters.

Public anger over housing reached a boiling point following the nationally televised eviction of an 87-year-old woman from her home in Madrid last month. The subsequent death of Maricarmen, as the woman became known, caused even more indignation and solidified her as a symbol of Spaniards who feel they pay too much on rent and can’t even dream of homeownership.

Housing activists leveraged the uproar over Maricarmen's eviction to call for the general strike. They soon won the backing of Spain's two main unions, UGT and CCOO.

The housing activists want several measures, including the elimination of tourist apartments, a crackdown on real estate speculation and protection for renters in the form of automatic renewals of leases.

The UGT and CCOO unions are demanding more government intervention in the housing market and a new minimum wage agreement through talks with the business owners' association.

articles.title: Immigration arrests go on unabated despite Trump's misgivings after GOP's midterm wipeout
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: After Democrats trounced GOP and won control of the next Congress, Donald Trump said his immigration crackdown may have been “too tough” and suggested it was time to sit down with the rival party
It's business as usual for President Donald Trump 's deportation offensive despite the Republican wipeout in the midterm elections.

In Los Angeles, masked immigration officers in body armour blocked a hospital emergency room driveway in a heavily Latino neighbourhood early Saturday (November 7, 2026). In central Alabama, twin 19-year-old brothers from Venezuela were arrested while driving back to college a day after the election.
Advocates reported arrests from California to Michigan to Massachusetts.
After Democrats trounced the GOP and won control of the next Congress, Mr. Trump said his immigration crackdown may have been “too tough” and suggested it was time to sit down with the rival party.
“I'd love to do something on immigration,” he said in an interview with CBS “60 Minutes” recorded Friday (November 6, 2026).

Hours later, he named Stephen Miller , the architect of his hardline immigration agenda, as his new chief of staff. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, meanwhile, said his orders had not changed.

“Deportations will continue,” Mr. Mullin wrote in an online post the day after the election, warning that U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement takes no days off and that “this includes on Thanksgiving, Christmas, and Election Day.”
María Bilbao, a campaign coordinator for the American Friends Service Committee in Miami, said she has received at least one call a day from someone detained in South Florida since the election.
“Everything remains exactly the same. The arrests have not ceased at all,” Ms. Bilbao said.

Florida Highway Patrol officers and ICE agents have detained people in their cars, as well as in places including supermarkets, pharmacies and gas stations. Immigrants under supervision have also been arrested when they showed up at ICE's Miami office for their appointments.

articles.title: Himalayas agenda left off COP31 formal list as major blocs withhold support: Nepal Foreign Minister
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Nepal's Minister of Foreign Affairs, said that the three countries would continue to face challenges in getting the issue formally recognised without the support of major countries

An agenda item on the Himalayas proposed by Nepal, Bhutan and Kyrgyzstan has not been included in the formal list of the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) after failing to secure the backing of the developed nations.
The COP 31 commenced on Monday (November 9, 2026) in Antalya, Turkiye. Agenda items refer to the list of topics that are formally taken up for discussion at the conference every year.

Speaking to PTI at COP31, Shisir Khanal, Nepal's Minister of Foreign Affairs, said on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) that the three countries would continue to face challenges in getting the issue formally recognised without the support of major countries.
He said some nations explicitly backed the proposal raised on Monday (November 9, 2026), while others remained reluctant.

“This is part of a big negotiation. Different major blocs did not support it, and that made it difficult for the agenda to go through. From our side, we pushed as hard as we could. There were different voices in the room. Some explicitly supported our agenda, while others were quite reluctant,” he said.
A source with direct knowledge of the discussions said developed nations did not show interest when the three countries formally pushed the proposal.

“The agenda focused on the Himalayas was clearly diluted, and it was the European Union which did not show any interest in this agenda. Even though the issue is not completely off the charts, a high-level dialogue is expected on it soon,” the source told PTI on condition of anonymity.
The source added that developing nations did not object to or block the proposal when it was raised.

Asked which countries supported the proposal, Mr. Khanal said several Least Developed Countries (LDCs) and mountain nations were positive, while developed countries were reluctant to take up a new agenda.

According to the Nepal government, a research dialogue is expected during the upcoming sessions at COP31, and the presidency has assured that a final text addressing mountain-related issues will be included in the conference's outcome document.

articles.title: WhatsApp to simplify communication on app, add financial services
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Meta’s head of WhatsApp Kunal Shah shared a post outlining some largely expected outcomes for the messaging platform
Meta’s new head of WhatsApp, Kunal Shah, has promised simplified calls/messages and more financial services on the messaging platform, apart from increased AI integration.
In a post on the social media platform X on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), Mr. Shah said he had spent around four months at WhatsApp.
He also shared some largely expected goals for the platform.
The WhatsApp executive said he would make voice notes, groups, stickers and video “simpler and more expressive.”

The company is also working with financial services and telecom partners to explore processes such as paying bills, borrowing money, and ensuring connectivity during travel. The aim of this step is to keep users within the messaging platform, even if they are completing other personal finance tasks.
Not surprisingly, Mr. Shah said he wanted to make these features more efficient with AI.
He did not announce any specific features or share a release date for the same.
WhatsApp handles over 100 billion messages and 2 billion calls every day, he shared, while stressing that the company’s principles would not change any time soon.

“Your personal messages and calls stay end-to-end encrypted. This and our quality bar stays the same. What happens inside WhatsApp only matters for what it makes possible outside it: more time together, stronger communities, and fewer barriers between people and the lives they want to live,” shared Mr. Shah.

Meta’s head of WhatsApp Kunal Shah shared a post outlining some largely expected outcomes for the messaging platform

Meta’s new head of WhatsApp, Kunal Shah, has promised simplified calls/messages and more financial services on the messaging platform, apart from increased AI integration.

In a post on the social media platform X on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), Mr. Shah said he had spent around four months at WhatsApp.

He also shared some largely expected goals for the platform.

The WhatsApp executive said he would make voice notes, groups, stickers and video “simpler and more expressive.”

The company is also working with financial services and telecom partners to explore processes such as paying bills, borrowing money, and ensuring connectivity during travel. The aim of this step is to keep users within the messaging platform, even if they are completing other personal finance tasks.

Not surprisingly, Mr. Shah said he wanted to make these features more efficient with AI.

He did not announce any specific features or share a release date for the same.

WhatsApp handles over 100 billion messages and 2 billion calls every day, he shared, while stressing that the company’s principles would not change any time soon.

“Your personal messages and calls stay end-to-end encrypted. This and our quality bar stays the same. What happens inside WhatsApp only matters for what it makes possible outside it: more time together, stronger communities, and fewer barriers between people and the lives they want to live,” shared Mr. Shah.

articles.title: Faith meets fitness: The Keralam church where prayers come with pull-ups
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: St. Joseph’s Church in Kuriachira, Thrissur, has set up an open gym to promote fitness among parishioners. With no fixed timings, parishioners can drop in at their convenience, with many heading to the gym after attending Holy Mass

At St. Joseph’s Church in Kuriachira, Thrissur, Keralam, faith and fitness go hand in hand. An open gym on the church premises is drawing parishioners of all ages to stretch, sweat and stay fit. The unusual initiative is adding a healthy new dimension to church life.

Set up in a corner of the church campus, the facility has quickly become a meeting point for fitness enthusiasts. With no fixed timings, parishioners can drop in at their convenience, with many heading to the gym after attending Holy Mass. The altar boys, numbering around 60, are among its regular users. Parents also bring their young children, while senior citizens use the basic equipment to stay active.

The initiative has its roots in the personal fitness routine of the church’s vicar, Fr. Frederick Eluvathingal, 69. A footballer and basketball player during his student days, he has never allowed age or a demanding schedule to come in the way of exercise.

“I have been working out for the past 51 years, ever since my days at the Papal Seminary in Pune,” he says. His fitness routine continued during his higher studies in Rome and Jerusalem and his church assignments in Australia.

When he arrived at Kuriachira more than a year ago, he began looking for a suitable space to continue his regular exercises, including push-ups and pull-ups. Parallel bars were installed first, followed by a basketball hoop. The idea gradually grew into a community gym.

“I wanted to create a space where people could develop the habit of working out. We generally do not have a strong workout culture. If people can fit in some basic exercise when they come to church, they may gradually make fitness part of their lives,” he says.

The need is particularly pressing at a time when lifestyle diseases and obesity are on the rise. The initiative also seeks to draw more youngsters into church activities and channel their energy into constructive pursuits.

The parish welcomed the proposal, and a space around a well on the church premises was chosen for the facility. The limited space available in Kuriachira meant that the gym had to be modest, but the response has been encouraging.
“Within a week of starting the gym, quite a few people began coming here. If the demand grows, we will have to think about expanding the facility,” says P.R. Wilson, one of the church trustees.

For regular user John Vazhappilly, a real estate broker who lives nearby, the gym has come as a timely help. “I have been coming here every evening for the past week. After an accident and surgery, the muscles in my leg became weak. I want to strengthen them. This is a comfortable place to exercise, with fresh air and an open campus,” he says.

articles.title: Congo's Ebola outbreak tops 11,000 cases as disease keeps spreading
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Since the outbreak was declared mid-May, Congolese authorities have struggled to contain it due to a series of factors including conflicts and a health system crisis
Congo's Ebola cases have crossed 11,000 cases in another development that shows the severity of the outbreak.

The latest Health Ministry data on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) showed 11,042 people have been infected by the deadly virus that has now killed 5,387, nearly half of those infected, in the country's deadliest outbreak.
Since the outbreak was declared mid-May, Congolese authorities have struggled to contain it due to a series of factors including conflicts and a health system crisis.
The Bundibugyo virus responsible for this outbreak has no known vaccine or treatment and has spread to the eight of the country's 26 Provinces.

Dozens of Ebola outbreaks have been reported since the disease was first discovered in 1976. The largest and deadliest occurred in West Africa from 2014 to 2016, with 28,000 infections and more than 11,000 deaths.

The current outbreak already ranks second, and has had at least three times the number of cases and deaths in the time since it was declared compared with the West Africa outbreak. Health officials declared the outbreak in May, but medical evidence suggests infections were occurring months earlier.

articles.title: What is Megaspeed International, the firm under scanner over Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang affair
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Megaspeed International has come under the scanner after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s alleged affair with Alice Huang, a woman accused of being a Chinese spy.

Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based cloud computing firm, is in the spotlight after the alleged extramarital affair of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang with one of the company’s former executives, Alice Huang. Ms Huang is accused of being a Chinese spy.

According to its website , Megaspeed is an Nvidia cloud partner in the Asia-Pacific region and a core business partner of Nvidia’s computing power cloud business. It adds that “we provide privatized, customized computing power product services covering NVIDIA’s entire GPU product line.”

A Reuters report says that Megaspeed International was incorporated in 2015 as 7Road International before changing its name to Megaspeed International in March 2023. It adds that the company is wholly owned by Singapore-registered Swiftdata, incorporated in October 2023, which says providing hosting services by non-data centers is its principal activity.

Reuters adds that Megaspeed’s assets increased sharply to $3 billion in 2024 from $33 million in 2023, its business filings showed. It reported an after-tax loss of $20 million ‌in ⁠2024, versus a loss of $21,283 a year earlier, while revenue jumped to $294 million from zero. Its cash flow statement showed $844,555 went to investing activities in 2024, after financing activities brought in cash of $10 million the previous year.

According to the company’s LinkedIn , it has around 2-10 employees and 23 associated members. The interactive map by LinkedIn shows that Megaspeed has offices in Iskandar Puteri, Malaysia; Senayan City, Indonesia; and is headquartered in the Central Region of Singapore.

Washington has restricted the export of Nvidia’s most cutting-edge silicon chips to China, citing national security concerns. The move is also seen as a measure to stay ahead in the field of artificial intelligence.
The New York Times has reported that the U.S. government has been probing Megaspeed since 2024 over its potential steering of Nvidia chips to China.
All of this, combined with the allegations of Ms Huang being a Chinese spy, has triggered speculation over Megaspeed’s involvement in the alleged chip transfer to China.

As per an AFP report, in 2025, Bloomberg News also reported on the Singaporean probe into Megaspeed over the alleged smuggling of Nvidia chips to China. According to AFP , Megaspeed retorted in December of the same year, saying that Bloomberg’s reporting “contains misleading information and incorrect insinuations, including suggestions that we may have been involved in illegal chip transfers”.

Jensen Huang, the top boss of the chip maker and one of the world’s most valuable publicly traded companies, has admitted to being unfaithful to his wife, without disclosing details of the alleged relationship with Alice Huang. The Nvidia CEO said that he was “deeply sorry” for the affair. “I was unfaithful to my wife, my actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did,” the statement, uploaded on Nvidia’s website added.

articles.title: Anthropic targets valuation of up to $1.4 trillion
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The stock market debut will be the first by one of the leading AI model developers

Anthropic plans to raise up to $64 billion in its upcoming initial public offering, the artificial intelligence giant said in a filing Tuesday, in a listing that could value the company at up to $1.4 trillion.
The stock market debut will be the first by one of the leading AI model developers and is being seen as a gauge of how long the AI spending boom lifting the US economy can last.

The maker of the Claude AI models said in a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission that it aims to sell 825 million shares at between $70 and $78 each. The shares will trade under the ticker "ANT."
Seven tech companies including Google, Nvidia, AMD and Microsoft have also agreed to buy $26 billion of non-voting shares at the IPO price in a separate private placement, the filing showed.
The companies are investors in Anthropic or major suppliers of its computing power.
Anthropic had been expected to raise up to $100 billion, which would have made it the largest IPO on record.
Even at the top of its price range, the offering would fall short of the record set by Elon Musk's SpaceX, which raised $86 billion in its June IPO at a valuation of $1.77 trillion.
Anthropic has been aiming to go public the week of November 16, and reports said its shares would begin trading on November 19.

Anthropic's listing is "just another chapter" in investors' worries over the cost of the AI buildout and how it gets financed, Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth Management, told AFP.

"But at the end of the day, I think there are three massive companies that investors have wanted to be part of for the last three years and that's SpaceX for sure, Anthropic is next, and perhaps next year OpenAI," he said.

The stock market debut will be the first by one of the leading AI model developers

Anthropic plans to raise up to $64 billion in its upcoming initial public offering, the artificial intelligence giant said in a filing Tuesday, in a listing that could value the company at up to $1.4 trillion.

The stock market debut will be the first by one of the leading AI model developers and is being seen as a gauge of how long the AI spending boom lifting the US economy can last.

The maker of the Claude AI models said in a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission that it aims to sell 825 million shares at between $70 and $78 each. The shares will trade under the ticker "ANT."

Seven tech companies including Google, Nvidia, AMD and Microsoft have also agreed to buy $26 billion of non-voting shares at the IPO price in a separate private placement, the filing showed.

The companies are investors in Anthropic or major suppliers of its computing power.

Anthropic had been expected to raise up to $100 billion, which would have made it the largest IPO on record.

Even at the top of its price range, the offering would fall short of the record set by Elon Musk's SpaceX, which raised $86 billion in its June IPO at a valuation of $1.77 trillion.

Anthropic has been aiming to go public the week of November 16, and reports said its shares would begin trading on November 19.

Anthropic's listing is "just another chapter" in investors' worries over the cost of the AI buildout and how it gets financed, Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth Management, told AFP.

"But at the end of the day, I think there are three massive companies that investors have wanted to be part of for the last three years and that's SpaceX for sure, Anthropic is next, and perhaps next year OpenAI," he said.

articles.title: Periyar Arivulagam book purchase row: DVAC launches probe in Tamil Nadu libraries
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The issue was flagged by award-winning Tamil writer Perumal Murugan who visited the library in Coimbatore recently and pointed to issues relating to price, quality and authenticity of content in some books.

The Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) has launched a detailed inquiry into allegations of serious financial irregularities at Anna Centenary Library in Chennai and Periyar Arivulagam library at Coimbatore .

DVAC officers perused records in both the libraries on Monday (November 9, 2026) and Tuesday (November 10) after registering the detailed inquiry which followed a statement made by Tamil Nadu School Education Minister Rajmohan alleging that irregularities took place during the erstwhile DMK regime in the purchase of books for the newly-launched Periyar Arivulagam library in Coimbatore.

Amidst allegations that books with AI-generated content and factual mistakes were purchased at inflated rates, DVAC officers made enquiries with the library staff and took copies of certain records in both the libraries for investigation, sources in the investigating agency said.
The controversy surrounding procurement of books for Periyar Arivulagam in Coimbatore | Explained
Periyar Arivulagam books row: People of Tamil Nadu will never forgive DMK for corruption, says CM Vijay
Library book ‘scam’: Madras High Court had sounded warning two years ago, called for enquiry

The issue was flagged by noted Tamil writer Perumal Murugan who visited the library in Coimbatore recently and pointed to issues relating to price, quality and authenticity of content in some books. The agency is looking into allegations of names of fictitious authors, fabrication of International Standard Book Number (ISBNs), depiction of factual errors and higher book prices.
During the search at Periyar Arivulagam in Coimbatore on Tuesday, DVAC sleuths scrutinised documents pertaining to book purchase in the administrative section of the library, on the third floor.
The DVAC would register a case if prima facie evidence is established in the detailed inquiry.

articles.title: Andhra Pradesh to spend Rs.632 crore on restoration of 789 lift irrigation schemes
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The restored schemes will provide irrigation to 7.49 lakh acres, officials tell Chief Minister Naidu

The Andhra Pradesh government will spend ₹632.07 crore on restoring 789 defunct lift irrigation schemes across the State, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu said, directing officials to complete all repairs by June 2027 to ensure their availability for the ensuing kharif season.

Reviewing irrigation projects and lift irrigation schemes at his camp office on Wednesday (November 11, 2026), Mr. Naidu instructed officials to undertake field inspections, call tenders immediately and commence repair works without delay. He said all 789 schemes identified for restoration must be made operational before the commencement of the agricultural season.

Officials informed the Chief Minister that the restoration works would require ₹632.07 crore and help provide irrigation facilities to 7.49 lakh acres. Mr. Naidu directed the Water Resources Department to establish a robust mechanism for the operation and maintenance of the schemes.

He asked the Jalaharathi Corporation to take up continuous monitoring of the lift irrigation schemes by setting up a dedicated division. If necessary, a Chief Engineer or Superintending Engineer should be appointed for each district to oversee their functioning and maintenance, he said.

The officials informed the Chief Minister that 4,061 acres had been identified out of 5,565 acres available with the Water Resources Department for setting up solar power plants. These installations could generate 877.3 MW of electricity.

articles.title: The controversy surrounding procurement of books for Periyar Arivulagam in Coimbatore | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The controversy caused a furore in Tamil Nadu, as the case heads into a Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption inquiry, court intervention and the scope of investigations has now explanded to include inventories in several other libraries

The story so far: A veritable pandora’s box of literary and political controversy was opened on November 6, 2026, when Sahitya Akademi winner Perumal Murugan wrote about several irregularities in the procurement of books for the newly-inaugurated Periyar Arivulagam library in Coimbatore. He wrote, and later spoke online, about how thousands of exorbitantly-priced books had been procured for the library with questionable authorship, full of factual errors and were seemingly AI generated. He also pointed out that these books had been procured at inflated rates, many times higher than current market rates for similar publications.

It has since caused a furore in Tamil Nadu, as the case heads into a Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption inquiry, court intervention and the scope of investigations has now explanded to include inventories in several other libraries, and it has also started an intense political blame game with the prime actors being the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) and its predecessor, now in the Opposition, the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam.
