articles.title: Congress launches ‘Punjab Mangda Insaaf’ campaign ahead of State polls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh and Leader of Opposition (LoP) in the State Assembly Partap Singh Bajwa launched the campaign at the party headquarters in Chandigarh
The Punjab Congress on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) rolled out 'Punjab Mangda Insaaf' campaign to reach out to every section of society and raise their concerns effectively ahead of the State polls.
Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh and Leader of Opposition (LoP) in the State Assembly Partap Singh Bajwa launched the campaign at the party headquarters in Chandigarh.
'Punjab Mangda Insaaf' is aimed at connecting with the people of Punjab and raising issues concerning farmers, youths, drugs, law and order and other public concerns, according to the party.
Speaking to reporters in Chandigarh, LoP Bajwa said that under this campaign, the Punjab Congress leadership will visit different parts of Punjab and raise issues concerning all sections of society.

"We will speak about the fraud with government employees and pensioners by the AAP government, the old pension scheme not being implemented, the law and order situation and the poor financial health of the State," he said.
Mr. Bajwa claimed the AAP government has failed on all fronts.

"AAP leader Arvind Kejriwal had promised Rs 54,000 crore funds per annum for setting up colleges, medical colleges, new infrastructure including roads, bridges. Not even a single penny was given. We will ask Kejriwal where that money has gone," he said.
"They did nothing for farmers, women or traders," he claimed.
Asked about Congress MP Charanjit Singh Channi's cycle yatra, which will commence on November 12, Mr. Bajwa said it is also part of the party's programme.
"Channi saab is our brother. With his programme, the message of the Congress will reach Punjab. We will do it together. We all will go there [cycle yatra] tomorrow as well," he said.

articles.title: God belongs to everyone, says Akhilesh on his Ayodhya visit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Claiming the BJP wins elections through dishonesty and fraud, the SP chief said that voters have made up their mind to bring his party to power in U.P.; he called for a voter list to be linked to Aadhaar

Dismissing the BJP’s criticism of his plans to visit Ayodhya next month, Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) emphasised that “God belongs to everyone” and slammed his critics for their alleged loot and destruction in Ayodhya.
Mr. Yadav is scheduled to visit the Ram Temple in Ayodhya on December 12, with his family. BJP leaders triggered a political war of words by terming his visit politically motivated.

Samajwadi Party National president Akhilesh Yadav celebrates the birthday of Khajanchi, the child who was born in a bank queue during demonetisation, by presenting him with gifts and cash during a press conference at the party office in Lucknow. | Photo Credit: ANI

“God belongs to everyone. So why should we not visit these places? We will visit Kedareshwar, Mathura and Vrindavan as well. We have been visiting these places before, and we will continue to do so. Those who looted and destroyed the livelihood of common people should answer,” Mr. Yadav told journalists in Lucknow.
The SP president claimed that Uttar Pradesh voters have determined to bring his party back into power in the State.

“The farmers, youth, labourers, and traders of Uttar Pradesh want change. The public has made up its mind to form the government of the Samajwadi Party in 2027. The people of the State are ready; the end of the BJP is near. Under the BJP government, injustice, oppression, inflation, and unemployment are at their peak. The Chief Minister is unaware of the employment rate and unemployment rate,” Mr. Yadav said, urging party workers to win booths and be vigilant.

“The BJP wins elections through dishonesty and fraud. The BJP wanted to commit dishonesty through the [special intensive revision] SIR process, but the workers of the Samajwadi Party and the PDA guards saved their votes. It is the responsibility of all leaders and workers to keep their votes safe and strengthen the booths,” he added.

The SP chief demanded that the voter list be linked with Aadhaar cards and said that these cards should be made of metal so that fakes cannot be created. “If everyone’s Aadhaar card is biometric, then why is the voter list not being linked to the Aadhaar card? When discussions are being held about Digital India and becoming equal to the world, why is the voter list not being linked to the Aadhaar card?” he asked.

Mr. Yadav claimed that the BJP was scared of the PDA, his acronym for an alliance of minorities, Dalits, and backward class voters. “Now the fight is not 80 versus 20, but 95 versus 5. This time in the Assembly elections, the BJP will not be visible on the ground. Seeing the BJP’s defeat, the Chief Minister’s language and behaviour have changed,” he said.
Celebrating the birthday of Khajanchi, a 10-year-old boy born during demonetisation in 2016, Mr. Yadav described ‘note bandi ’ as the most corrupt decision in the world’s history.

Claiming the BJP wins elections through dishonesty and fraud, the SP chief said that voters have made up their mind to bring his party to power in U.P.; he called for a voter list to be linked to Aadhaar

Dismissing the BJP’s criticism of his plans to visit Ayodhya next month, Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) emphasised that “God belongs to everyone” and slammed his critics for their alleged loot and destruction in Ayodhya.

Mr. Yadav is scheduled to visit the Ram Temple in Ayodhya on December 12, with his family. BJP leaders triggered a political war of words by terming his visit politically motivated.

Samajwadi Party National president Akhilesh Yadav celebrates the birthday of Khajanchi, the child who was born in a bank queue during demonetisation, by presenting him with gifts and cash during a press conference at the party office in Lucknow. | Photo Credit: ANI

“God belongs to everyone. So why should we not visit these places? We will visit Kedareshwar, Mathura and Vrindavan as well. We have been visiting these places before, and we will continue to do so. Those who looted and destroyed the livelihood of common people should answer,” Mr. Yadav told journalists in Lucknow.

The SP president claimed that Uttar Pradesh voters have determined to bring his party back into power in the State.

“The farmers, youth, labourers, and traders of Uttar Pradesh want change. The public has made up its mind to form the government of the Samajwadi Party in 2027. The people of the State are ready; the end of the BJP is near. Under the BJP government, injustice, oppression, inflation, and unemployment are at their peak. The Chief Minister is unaware of the employment rate and unemployment rate,” Mr. Yadav said, urging party workers to win booths and be vigilant.

“The BJP wins elections through dishonesty and fraud. The BJP wanted to commit dishonesty through the [special intensive revision] SIR process, but the workers of the Samajwadi Party and the PDA guards saved their votes. It is the responsibility of all leaders and workers to keep their votes safe and strengthen the booths,” he added.

The SP chief demanded that the voter list be linked with Aadhaar cards and said that these cards should be made of metal so that fakes cannot be created. “If everyone’s Aadhaar card is biometric, then why is the voter list not being linked to the Aadhaar card? When discussions are being held about Digital India and becoming equal to the world, why is the voter list not being linked to the Aadhaar card?” he asked.

Mr. Yadav claimed that the BJP was scared of the PDA, his acronym for an alliance of minorities, Dalits, and backward class voters. “Now the fight is not 80 versus 20, but 95 versus 5. This time in the Assembly elections, the BJP will not be visible on the ground. Seeing the BJP’s defeat, the Chief Minister’s language and behaviour have changed,” he said.

Celebrating the birthday of Khajanchi, a 10-year-old boy born during demonetisation in 2016, Mr. Yadav described ‘note bandi ’ as the most corrupt decision in the world’s history.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy on Wednesday said the first phase of the Musi rejuvenation project would begin shortly, asserting that the river had to be cleaned up and restored rather than merely beautified. He said the government would ensure that no one suffers losses in the process and called for the cooperation of all political parties.

Speaking at the inauguration of the revived Thammidikunta Lake, he said Musi river pollution was causing hardships to people in Nalgonda district, who were paying the price for the neglect of successive governments. The lives of Hyderabad residents were closely linked to the river, he said.

Recalling the construction of Osmansagar and Himayatsagar reservoirs by the Nizam to protect Hyderabad from floods, he said the Musi riverfront had been developed nearly a century ago, but the water body had now become polluted.

Describing Hyderabad as a city of rocks and lakes, Mr. Revanth Reddy said it had 1,372 lakes, but nearly 50% had disappeared due to various reasons. Encroachments had resulted in waterlogging on roads and flooding of residential colonies during rains. He stressed the need to free lakes from encroachments as part of efforts to protect nature and establish Hyderabad as a global city.

He said Thammidikunta Lake had been expanded from 14 to 30 acres, keeping the future of coming generations in mind, even if some people suffered losses in the process. Actor Akkineni Nagarjuna had voluntarily handed over two acres of land to the government, he said, describing him as a hero in real life as well as in films.

The Chief Minister said the lake would become a new destination alongside Shilparamam and called for developing a lake economy around it. He directed police officials to ensure adequate security and suggested planting a Jammi tree on the lake premises so that lakes could become venues for Dasara celebrations and help preserve cultural traditions.

articles.title: Assam CM Himanta Sarma backs woman’s paternity case against ex-Uttarakhand Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Ms. Indira Dewri has renewed her demand for a fresh CBI probe and DNA test to establish the paternity of her 23-year-old son
Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma has backed a woman’s demand for justice in a 23-year-old paternity row involving former Uttarakhand Minister and Congress leader Harak Singh Rawat.
In a social media post on Wednesday (November 11, 2026), the Chief Minister said he had met Ms. Indira Dewri, also known as Jenny, who claims that Mr. Rawat raped and impregnated her in 2003.

Condemning the treatment Ms. Dewri — who hails from Sadiya in Assam’s Tinsukia district — had received, Mr. Sarma wrote: “Yesterday (November 10, 2026), I met Jenny, a resident of Assam. What a man named Harak Singh Rawat from Uttarakhand did to her is extremely wrong and reprehensible. No one should have to suffer the kind of cruelty she endured. I stand firmly with her in this fight for justice.”
In the meeting, Ms. Dewri renewed her demand for a DNA test and a fresh Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe to establish the paternity of her 23-year-old son.
She told journalists in Dehradun on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) that she has appealed to Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami for justice.
She would stay in Dehradun until her demands were addressed, she said.
Ms. Dewri criticised the earlier CBI investigation, alleging the agency had not recorded her statement properly. She also said the CBI did not collect samples from her son for a DNA test.
“I have received threats. I need protection,” she said, while also insisting on a narco-analysis.
Mr. Rawat denied the allegations, including the charge of rape, and challenged those involved to undergo DNA tests under court supervision.
He accused the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of reviving the controversy to target him and the Congress party ahead of State Assembly elections slated for 2027.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: While some of the former CM’s supporters gathered at her residence, most of her erstwhile loyalists were conspicuous by their absence

Former West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) skipped the Bhai Phonta festivities at her residence, breaking a tradition going back several years when leaders of her party would make a beeline to seek her blessing.

Celebrated as Bhai Dooj in other parts of India, sisters apply a tika on their brothers’ foreheads as a mark of love, and pray for their long and healthy lives. Ms. Banerjee, who is also called ‘ Didi’ (elder sister), would offer the tilak to a number of her party leaders and supporters.

“Mamata di is not observing Bhai Phonta. She did not observe Bijoya [Vijayadasami] before. She will not observe Bhai Phonta this time either. In light of the attacks, terror, police brutality and arrests on false charges that TMC [Trinamool Congress] workers have faced since the elections, @MamataOfficial did not observe Bijoya this time,” Mamata All India Trinamool Congress (AITC) spokesperson Kunal Ghosh said.

“Since the family’s Kali Puja could not be cancelled, Ms. Banerjee performed the puja for the goddess. But she will not hold any Bhai Phonta ceremony. Anyone may come to see her. But Didi will not hold a Bhai Phonta ceremony this time,” Mr. Ghosh said.

While some of Ms. Banerjee’s supporters gathered at her residence, most of her erstwhile loyalists, who have since deserted her, were conspicuous by their absence. AITC leader and Sreerampur MP Kalyan Banerjee, who visited her residence, criticised the “opportunists who would come during Bhai Phonta” when she was in power. The Chief Minister had raised her brothers all by herself, the MP said.

The remarks by came in the context of Ms. Banerjee’s youngest brother, Swapan Banerjee, meeting Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Tuesday (November 11, 2026) evening. Mr. Swapan Banerjee was seen touching Mr. Adhikari’s feet and heaping praise on the Chief Minister. Mr. Adhikari had visited Kalighat to participate in a Kali Puja organised by locals. Mr. Swapan Banerjee also said that he would not attend Bhai Phonta at his sister’s residence.

On Wednesday (November 11, 2026) , Mr. Swapan Banerjee joined the leaders of the party’s rebel faction, who held a Bhai Phonta event at the office of the Democratic Trinamool Congress (DTP). Leaders of the DTP, including Ritabrata Banerjee and Madan Mitra, were present when the former Chief Minister’s brother joined them. Chandrima Bhattacharya, a former Minister in Ms. Banerjee’s Cabinet, was seen offering Bhai Phonta to leaders of the rebel TMC faction.

articles.title: CM Vijay urges TVK MLAs to stay united, prioritise public grievances, avoid controversies
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: His meeting with the party MLAs assumes significance against the backdrop of his government completing six months in office and some legislators recently getting involved in controversies

Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) president and Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) held a meeting with his party MLAs for nearly three hours at a private resort near Mamallapuram in Chengalpattu district and urged them to stay united, work for the people and refrain from getting involved in controversies.

His meeting with the party MLAs assumes significance against the backdrop of his government completing six months in office and some legislators recently getting involved in controversies. Barring a few legislators, the majority of the legislators participated in the meeting.

Sources who attended the meeting told The Hindu that Mr. Vijay interacted with the MLAs in batches of 10, spending nearly 10 to 15 minutes with each batch. He first held discussions with the women MLAs of the party. Later, he interacted with the other MLAs and finally with the Ministers.

Sources said Mr. Vijay conveyed Deepavali greetings to the MLAs and distributed saris and dhotis to them. Some MLAs were learnt to have raised the issue of not being able to meet him frequently and of non-cooperation from officials. The Chief Minister took note of their concerns and told them to bring forward grievances from their respective Assembly constituencies and meet him at the Secretariat.

He also urged the party MLAs to stay united and refrain from getting involved in any controversies. He is also learnt to have told them that the Opposition parties might attempt to create controversies and cautioned them to remain vigilant.

articles.title: Amid call for Ladakh protest, CEO prohibits dharnas in Leh, Kargil over upcoming polls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The order came a day after Ladakh’s civil society groups announced that agitations to push a slew of demands would resume on November 12

With Ladakh’s civil society groups threatening to resume agitations to push a slew of demands, the Union Territory’s Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) issued an order prohibiting all dharnas, protests, demonstrations, sit-ins and rallies within the municipal limits of Leh and Kargil while the Model Code of Conduct is in force ahead of local body elections.
The order said the restrictions will remain in force until the completion of the election process for the municipal committees of Leh and Kargil this month.

“The Model Code requires maintenance of an atmosphere conducive to free, fair and peaceful elections, and no activity should be permitted which may create intimidation, fear or undue influence among electors,” said the order.

It said organising political dharnas, protests, demonstrations, sit-ins, rallies, or similar collective activities during this period would have the potential to intimidate voters, disturb public order, and vitiate the atmosphere for free and fair elections.

It directed all political parties, candidates, and their agents to strictly adhere to the provisions of the Model Code of Conduct and ensure no activity is undertaken that may intimidate, coerce, or unduly influence electors.
The District Election Officers, or Deputy Commissioners, of Leh and Kargil and the Superintendents of Police of the districts were directed “to ensure strict compliance of the order”.
“Any violation will be dealt with firmly in accordance with law, including proceedings under relevant provisions and the Model Code of Conduct,” it added.

The order came a day after Leh Apex Body (LAB) called for an agitation, with a sit-in from November 12, to press their demands on a slew of issues, including the resumption of talks between the Centre and Ladakh bodies, making public the status of the judicial inquiry report into the September 24, 2025, violence that left four people dead, and the postponement of hill council elections till next year.

Members of the LAB, including co-chairman Tsering Dorjey Lakrook and activist Sonam Wangchuk, on Wednesday made a video appeal to President Droupadi Murmu, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah, and the Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi “to intervene before people of Ladakh are forced to start peaceful but intense agitations to demonstrate our pain”.

“While the judicial inquiry commission report on the September 24 incidents in Leh moves at a snail’s pace even after a year of the incident, and the talks on restoration of democracy have broken down, the U.T. administration is moving at rocket speed to conduct some kind of council elections here, apparently to have people of their choice installed to negotiate on democracy and safeguards here,” said Mr. Wancghuk.

articles.title: Two days past Deepavali, NPCI yet to announce a date for UPI MDR rollout
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: About a month ago, when the NPCI had pushed back the rollout of MDR from its original date of October 15, it had said it would be implemented “immediately post Diwali”

Two days since Deepavali, the National Payments Council of India is yet to notify a new date for the implementation of the Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on UPI transactions and The Hindu has learnt that “there is no announcement on this at the moment”.

When it had put the proposed additional charge on hold nearly a month ago, the NPCI had said the new date would be announced “immediately” after Deepavali. The new rate was originally supposed to have been implemented on October 15.
“There is no announcement on this at the moment,” a spokesperson at the NPCI told The Hindu when asked whether the NPCI’s date announcement was imminent.

The matter of an MDR levy on specified UPI transactions received significant pushback from merchants and petrol pump dealers alike, apart from customers who feared that merchants would pass on the extra charge on to them by way of higher prices.
The petrol pump dealers further said that the MDR charge, coupled with the fact that their dealer commission had not been revised in several years, meant that their margins would be further squeezed.

The NPCI had on October 13 announced that its UPI and Services Steering Committee had decided that “keeping in mind the festive season, Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on select Person-to-Merchant (P2M) UPI transactions, shall be implemented immediately post Diwali at a date to be notified separately”.

The Hindu had at the time reported that, according to government sources, the decision to delay the implementation of MDR on UPI was made in the Prime Minister’s Office following strong appeals from traders.

Praveen Khandelwal, founder and secretary-general of the Confederation of All India Traders (CAIT) and a Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) Lok Sabha member, had welcomed the deferment, saying that it would protect traders’ interests and sustain digital payment momentum during the festive season.

articles.title: Militants ambush police vehicles in northwestern Pakistan, killing at least 10 officers
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Police say militants have ambushed vehicles carrying police officers in northwestern Pakistan, triggering a gunbattle that killed at least 10 officers
Militants ambushed vehicles carrying police officers in northwestern Pakistan on Wednesday (November 11, 2026), triggering a gunbattle that killed at least 10 officers, officials said.
The attack took place in Kohat, a district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, which borders Afghanistan, local police official Faisal Khan said.
He said two senior police officers were among the dead and an exchange of fire between security forces and the attackers was ongoing. He provided no further details.

Hours later, the Pakistani Taliban in a statement claimed the attack. The Pakistani Taliban, who were formerly known as Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan, or TTP, have stepped up attacks on security forces in the region in recent months.

Pakistan has seen a surge in violence in recent years, much of it blamed on the TTP. The group is separate from but closely allied with the Afghan Taliban, who returned to power in neighboring Afghanistan in 2021.

articles.title: German military to stop using Chinese-made drones, citing security concerns
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Drones from Chinese manufacturers had previously been permitted as a cost-effective option for target practice and training purposes; they will now be replaced with European products

Germany's military will no longer use Chinese-made drones, ​a defence ministry spokesperson said on Wednesday, amid mounting concern ‌among Western militaries that they could pose a ​security risk and be used to transmit ⁠sensitive information to Beijing.

Drones from Chinese manufacturers had previously been permitted as a cost-effective option for target practice and training purposes, ‌the spokesperson said. They will now be replaced with European products.
"To strengthen the Bundeswehr's ‌self-sufficiency and technological sovereignty, Chinese-made models will no ‌longer ⁠be used," the spokesperson said in an emailed ⁠statement.

There is no blanket ban on the use of systems from specific countries, the spokesperson said, adding the decision is based on ​individual risk assessments ‌aimed at safeguarding military security, IT and data security.
China's foreign ministry told Reuters that it opposed Germany's "discriminatory practice" targeting Chinese products.
Germany's Der Spiegel news outlet first ‌reported the change.

Local commanders had been allowed ​to purchase the drones under a 2024 strategy that included a "white list" of approved systems, ⁠including several made by China-based DJI, the world's largest drone maker, Spiegel reported.

DJI has repeatedly said its ‌drones do not pose a security risk and in May the company told US lawmakers that an independent review had found "no evidence of data transmission outside the United States".

The US last month prohibited vehicles made by China's BYD on its air base on Japan's ‌Okinawa island, and Poland in February banned Chinese-made vehicles from ​military facilities over concerns their sensors could be used to collect sensitive data.

The spokesperson said the ⁠German defence ministry had no general ban on vehicles from ⁠specific countries or manufacturers, but said sensors installed in modern vehicles are seen as potential security ‌risks, and therefore access to sensitive military sites can be restricted where necessary.

articles.title: DR Congo Ebola outbreak exceeds 11,000 cases, causes 5,387 deaths
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The 17th outbreak of the virus in the DRC's history was officially declared in May, but experts believe it emerged weeks or even months earlier

The Democratic Republic of Congo's worst-ever outbreak of Ebola has now reached more than 11,000 confirmed cases, official Congolese figures showed on Wednesday (November 11, 2026), as armed conflict hampers the response.
The 17th outbreak of the virus in the DRC's history was officially declared in May, but experts believe it emerged weeks or even months earlier.
It has infected 11,042 people in the DRC and caused 5,387 deaths, according to the National Institute of Public Health.
Around 2,990 people have recovered from Ebola, which is transmitted through contact with bodily fluids and causes severe hemorrhagic fever.
Ebola has killed more than 15,000 people in Africa over the last 50 years.
The worst outbreak previously recorded in the DRC killed nearly 2,300 people out of 3,500 cases between 2018 and 2020.
The latest outbreak began in northeastern Ituri province and has since spread to seven other provinces, with most cases concentrated in Ituri and North Kivu.
Cases have also been reported in Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria.
No approved vaccines or treatments exist currently for the Bundibugyo species of Ebola behind the latest outbreak.

Last month, the World Health Organization announced that Ervebo, a vaccine approved for use against the more common Zaire strain of Ebola, would be put through a full human trial in the DRC to see if it offered any cross-protection against Bundibugyo.

articles.title: COP31 leaders urge focus on climate action despite global conflicts
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Negotiators from nearly 200 countries are seeking agreement at COP31 on a proposal from Turkey to increase the share of electricity in global ‌energy use and revive stalled efforts to move away from fossil fuels

Wars and trade disputes should not be allowed to distract the world from ​its struggle to combat global warming, the leaders of Brazil and Turkey told the COP31 climate conference ⁠on Wednesday (November 11, 2026).

"A year ago, the planet left COP30 invigorated... (but) this momentum has dropped off at the start of this year. Climate change disappeared from the speeches and documents from global leadership," Brazil's President Luiz ‌Inacio Lula da Silva, whose country hosted last year's conference, told the summit.
"We started talking more about weapons ‌and ⁠tariffs than the survival of future generations," he said. "The planet cannot be in the mercy of ⁠hegemonic struggles."
"Wars, crises, migration, famine and poverty increase the need for international solidarity each day," he said.
The U.S. and Israeli war on Iran this year has disrupted West Asia crude oil shipments and sent fuel prices soaring around the ​globe, triggering a scramble for reliable supplies.

Those dynamics ‌have pushed global warming down the list of urgent priorities for some governments, even as climate advocates argue they make the perfect case for a more rapid adoption of clean energy alternatives to oil.

Negotiators from nearly 200 countries are seeking agreement at COP31 on a proposal from Turkey to increase the share of electricity in global ‌energy use and revive stalled efforts to move away from fossil fuels.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres told ​world leaders earlier in the day that the slow international response to climate change so far had placed the world on a path to destruction, and that fast action was needed to ⁠avert it.

"The brutal truth is that the climate crisis is outrunning us. This is the path to mutually assured destruction," Mr. Guterres said, pointing to rising emissions, global temperatures and worsening climate-driven disasters.

A UN report last month found ‌the world on course to break through the 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) warming limit that countries had agreed to pursue under the Paris Agreement to prevent the worst effects of climate change.

articles.title: ‘Iran will not allow enriched nuclear material to leave the country’
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Rezaei has ‌said ⁠there are currently no negotiations taking place between Tehran ⁠and Washington

Iran will not allow even a single ​particle of enriched nuclear material to leave the country, and there ‌will be consequences in the event of any ​new U.S. strikes on the Islamic Republic, Iranian ⁠security chief Mohsen Rezaei said in televised remarks.

Mr. Rezaei was speaking to Lebanon's pro-Iranian Al Mayadeen TV after U.S. officials downplayed the need ‌for additional military action against Iran, with analysts noting President Donald Trump's more conciliatory tone since the ‌Republicans' defeat in the November 3 midterm elections.
Mr. Rezaei has ‌said ⁠there are currently no negotiations taking place between Tehran ⁠and Washington.
"Any new U.S. attacks will also be met with targeting U.S. bases far away," he said.
Iran's Supreme Leader has issued a directive ​that the country's near-weapons-grade uranium ‌should not be sent abroad, two senior Iranian sources said in May.

"We need the enriched material to design ships and submarines that work on nuclear energy", Mr. Rezaei said, ‌adding that Tehran has informed Moscow that its enriched ​nuclear material will remain in the country and "we will use it ourselves".
Russia has previously offered to ⁠remove uranium from Iran as part of a potential deal to ease U.S. concerns, but said it was for Tehran to ‌decide whether to remove it or not.

The IAEA estimates that Iran had 440.9 kg of uranium enriched to 60% — a level far higher than needed for civilian use — when Israel and the U.S. attacked Iranian nuclear facilities in June 2025. How much of that has survived is ‌unclear.
Israel, the United States and other Western countries have long accused Iran ​of seeking nuclear weapons. Iran denies the accusation.
Washington has said nuclear issues must be part of ⁠any initial negotiations with Iran aimed at ending the war between the ⁠two countries.

Mr. Rezaei was speaking to Lebanon's pro-Iranian Al Mayadeen TV after U.S. officials downplayed the need ‌for additional military action against Iran, with analysts noting President Donald Trump's more conciliatory tone since the ‌Republicans' defeat in the November 3 midterm elections.

Russia has previously offered to ⁠remove uranium from Iran as part of a potential deal to ease U.S. concerns, but said it was for Tehran to ‌decide whether to remove it or not.

Israel, the United States and other Western countries have long accused Iran ​of seeking nuclear weapons. Iran denies the accusation.

articles.title: Central committee suggests three-year roadmap to phase out unsustainable sand mining from active river channels
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: In its report, the CEC observes that while sand and gravel are crucial ingredients for infrastructure and construction, their unscientific or excessive extraction from active channels and floodplains disrupts the delicate dynamic balance of river systems

The Supreme Court-appointed Central Empowered Committee (CEC) has suggested preparing a time-bound roadmap to phase out unsustainable sand extraction from active river channels over the next three years.

The committee, a statutory body since 2023 and originally formed in 2002 on the apex court's order, has also recommended developing sustainable alternative sources of sand and aggregates to progressively reduce dependence on extraction from active river channels.
For this, it has suggested scientific desiltation of dams and reservoirs and recycling of construction and demolition (C&D) waste, among other measures.
These recommendations are part of the CEC's report submitted to the Supreme Court on November 2 as part of a sou motu case related to illegal sand mining in the National Chambal Sanctuary.

In its report, the CEC observes that while sand and gravel are crucial ingredients for infrastructure and construction, their unscientific or excessive extraction from active channels and floodplains disrupts the delicate dynamic balance of river systems.

"The impacts inter alia include riverbed degradation and infrastructure vulnerability, depletion of groundwater and loss of aquifers, destruction of aquatic and riparian habitats, and alteration of river morphology and hydrology, etc," said the committee.
It also highlights that there is no consolidated, reliable national database that quantifies the volume or value of illegally extracted river sand.
As a result, the CEC has recommended strengthening the existing regulatory and monitoring framework governing extraction from permissible areas.

This can be done through scientific identification of mineable stretches, regular replenishment studies, determination of sustainable extraction limits, environmental safeguards, digital tracking of mineral transportation and end-use and effective enforcement, it said.

"A time-bound roadmap shall be prepared to progressively phase out unsustainable sand extraction from active river channels over the next three years, alongside development of adequate alternative sources, including reservoir sediment, M-sand and recycled C&D waste, while ensuring that legitimate construction requirements are met,” the CEC said in its report.

articles.title: Prix Pascal: If AI writes your book, are you still a writer?
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: France’s new Prix Pascal for AI-assisted books prompts a writer to reflect on the slow pleasures of making art, loss of individuality, and need to reclaim human imagination

There is now a new French literary prize for AI-assisted writing — the Prix Pascal de Littérature IA. The Pascal prize requires entrants to turn in an unpublished manuscript, fiction or non-fiction, in French, of approximately 3,00,000 characters, written with the help of large language models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini. Writers must declare which AI model and prompts they have employed. The applications, to be submitted by November 30, consist of “a seed, a manuscript and a technical file, submitted simultaneously”. Ten finalists will be announced on December 4 and the winner will be revealed on December 15.

“This [submitted] work must be useful, or raise awareness, or help to solve in an original way one of the ecological, social and ethical challenges that threaten humanity. AI can now solve previously unsolvable mathematical problems. Here, it is asked to produce a text that will help humanity progress towards wisdom and the preservation of itself and its environment.”

I love the way in which the manifesto strategically reframes tacit support for what goes against the very grain of the creative spirit as an essentially moral and ethical act. But of course! This is the way these things are usually done. The prize was founded by Philippe Rodriguez, Albin Serviant and Gilles Mentré. The first two are technology entrepreneurs, which too is no surprise.

Notwithstanding their precarity, writers and artists have always been viewed with a combination of envy, fear and hatred. The imagination is a dangerous thing. It is ungovernable. It cannot easily be controlled or colonised. It does not seek permission. And that, to many, is frightening. What better way to colonise the imagination than to introduce AI into the writer’s world? Also, that way everybody — even the ones with little understanding of what a writer does — can acquire the overnight label of one. Where does this leave writers who have spent years honing their craft, writers who have survived by the skin of their teeth? The world needs writers more urgently than ever before, and more of us should let some form of creative practice into our lives.

Two semesters ago, a few students from my Creative Writing course, at Shiv Nadar University, Chennai, confessed to what their worst fears were: that, having come of age in the post-AI era, they would find it a challenge to access and exercise their imagination — which, in their understanding, was foundational to the course. I was struck by their capacity for self-reflection, moved by what they recognised, quite rightly, as an imminent loss. This, too, is the other dark side of what we have got ourselves into: the loss of imagination is foundational not just to the stray creative writing course but to life itself.

The argument that it is best not to be left behind, that AI is here to stay so writers must take the good things it has to offer and navigate the rest, is a specious one. The folks making this argument may be right about the inevitability of AI, but does that make any of it less disturbing or a tad more ethical? I don’t see how one can frame this as anything other than a pure black-and-white story. If you give AI an inch, it is very likely that you will take a mile from yourself.

It is a slippery slope. You start by using AI as an instrument — perhaps to help you rewrite a sentence — and before you know it, you are likely to seek its help extensively to write the entire piece. Who then is the real author of the piece? After all, it is in the writing that writers do their thinking. I don’t think the answer lies in declaring AI use upfront. While this may address the ethical question to a small extent, it still does not change the fact that we are always going to ‘writing’ with training wheels on. The craft is in the writing and if you give that away what is left?

There is another problem too: that of the asymmetry between the writer on whose work an LLM is trained and the user who then draws on that work to write in “collaboration with” that particular AI model. The original writer whose consent has very likely not been sought gets nothing from this entire process — a process which de-humanises creative work and repurposes it as training data.

Artificial intelligence illustrations are seen on a lapto with books in the background in this illustration photo on 18 July, 2023. (Photo by Jaap Arriens/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | Photo Credit: Getty Images

As almost everyone from editors of literary journals on the brink of closure to writing teachers will tell you, it is often impossible to tell AI-assisted writing apart from human writing. In fact, you may find that some AI-assisted writing may be as good as if not better than writing by humans. It, of course, depends on the prompts used and how advanced the models are.

It cannot easily be controlled or colonised. It does not seek permission. And that, to many, is frightening. What better way to colonise the imagination than to introduce AI into the writer’s world? Also, that way everybody — even the ones with little understanding of what a writer does — can acquire the overnight label of one. Where does this leave writers who have spent years honing their craft, writers who have survived by the skin of their teeth? The world needs writers more urgently than ever before, and more of us should let some form of creative practice into our lives.

Two semesters ago, a few students from my Creative Writing course, at Shiv Nadar University, Chennai, confessed to what their worst fears were: that, having come of age in the post-AI era, they would find it a challenge to access and exercise their imagination — which, in their understanding, was foundational to the course. I was struck by their capacity for self-reflection, moved by what they recognised, quite rightly, as an imminent loss. This, too, is the other dark side of what we have got ourselves into: the loss of imagination is foundational not just to the stray creative writing course but to life itself.

The argument that it is best not to be left behind, that AI is here to stay so writers must take the good things it has to offer and navigate the rest, is a specious one. The folks making this argument may be right about the inevitability of AI, but does that make any of it less disturbing or a tad more ethical? I don’t see how one can frame this as anything other than a pure black-and-white story. If you give AI an inch, it is very likely that you will take a mile from yourself.

It is a slippery slope. You start by using AI as an instrument — perhaps to help you rewrite a sentence — and before you know it, you are likely to seek its help extensively to write the entire piece. Who then is the real author of the piece? After all, it is in the writing that writers do their thinking. I don’t think the answer lies in declaring AI use upfront. While this may address the ethical question to a small extent, it still does not change the fact that we are always going to ‘writing’ with training wheels on. The craft is in the writing and if you give that away what is left?

There is another problem too: that of the asymmetry between the writer on whose work an LLM is trained and the user who then draws on that work to write in “collaboration with” that particular AI model. The original writer whose consent has very likely not been sought gets nothing from this entire process — a process which de-humanises creative work and repurposes it as training data.

Artificial intelligence illustrations are seen on a lapto with books in the background in this illustration photo on 18 July, 2023. (Photo by Jaap Arriens/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | Photo Credit: Getty Images

As almost everyone from editors of literary journals on the brink of closure to writing teachers will tell you, it is often impossible to tell AI-assisted writing apart from human writing. In fact, you may find that some AI-assisted writing may be as good as if not better than writing by humans. It, of course, depends on the prompts used and how advanced the models are.

articles.title: New registration framework proposed to strengthen allied and healthcare professions in India
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions invites public and stakeholder comments on the Draft Provisional Registration of Allied and Healthcare Professionals Regulations, 2026

The National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions (NCAHP), under the Union Ministry of Health, has proposed a comprehensive regulatory framework for the registration of allied and healthcare professionals, with pathways for skill upgradation, competency assessment, and transition to regular registration.

The broad categories of allied and healthcare professions governed by the NCAHP include clinical laboratories, surgical and emergency technology, physiotherapy, nutrition, ophthalmology, occupational therapy, community and behavioural health, medical imaging, physician associates, and health informatics.

The proposed framework aims for uniformity, transparency and accountability in professional registration. Practitioners can enhance their competencies in keeping with prescribed standards, a release issued by the Ministry said.
Key features of the proposed regulations include the establishment of a standardised mechanism for provisional registration in accordance with the NCAHP Act, 2021.

“Importantly, the proposed Regulations also provide opportunities for eligible provisionally registered professionals to undertake prescribed bridge courses for skill enhancement, supervised clinical training and minimum qualifying examinations, wherever applicable, to meet the requirements for regular registration,’’ the Healthy Ministry’s statement said.
This competency-based approach seeks to facilitate professional development and career progression, and improve the quality of allied and healthcare services.
“The proposed framework places emphasis on skill development, professional competence and regulatory accountability,’’ a senior Health Ministry official said.

By linking progression to regular registration with prescribed requirements, the regulations seek to ensure allied and healthcare professionals possess the necessary knowledge and clinical competencies to deliver quality healthcare services.
An integrated online registration system for submitting applications, verifying credentials, assess eligibility, and issue provisional registration certificates is also proposed.

Eligible professionals granted provisional registration will receive a Provisional Registration Unique Identification Number (PR UID). The digital platform will simply procedures, improve access, and promote uniform efficiency across States and Union Territories.

articles.title: Anaemia prevention in India: pivoting towards better multidimensional strategies
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: If anaemia reduction should align with India’s goals for NCD reduction, then the focus must be on better diets through diversification. That should be non-negotiable for public health policy: no amount of papering over cracks with pills and potions will work in the long term

India has had decades of unchanged high anaemia prevalence in women and children that has historically been thought to be due to iron deficiency. This has led firstly to an iron and folic acid (IFA) tablet supplementation targeted at women and children, and secondly to fitful implementation of mandatory fortification of staple foods. IFA is a ‘precision’ strategy, applying as it does to the vulnerable population it is intended for, while fortification is a broad strategy that applies to the entire population. The latter works in controlled settings such as clinical trials, but has not worked in real-world settings, and might have adverse effects when given to those it is unintended for.

The reason for pivoting: anaemia is mistakenly conflated with iron deficiency In India. The evidence is otherwise: in national Indian surveys, it has been shown that iron deficiency is not the major cause of anaemia. Indeed, fully one-third of anaemia cases demonstrate no micronutrient deficiency or obvious cause. Even so, giving iron should have sorted out those who did have iron deficiency anaemia, and reduced the general anaemia prevalence. While this could be a problem with inefficient programme implementation, two important questions arise: is there is really a deficiency in dietary iron intake in India? And is the administered iron being adequately absorbed and utilised for haemoglobin formation?

Science, Space & Environment Report: Anaemia prevention in India: pivoting towards better multidimensional strategies. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

articles.keyPoints:
• If anaemia reduction should align with India’s goals for NCD reduction, then the focus must be on better diets through diversification. That should be non-negotiable for public health policy: no amount of papering over cracks with pills and potions will work in the long term
• India has had decades of unchanged high anaemia prevalence in women and children that has historically been thought to be due to iron deficiency. This has led firstly to an iron and folic acid (IFA) tablet supplementation targeted at women and children, and secondly to fitful implementation of mandatory fortification of staple foods. IFA is a ‘precision’ strategy, applying as it does to the vulnerable population it is intended for, while fortification is a broad strategy that applies to the entire population. The latter works in controlled settings such as clinical trials, but has not worked in real-world settings, and might have adverse effects when given to those it is unintended for.
• The reason for pivoting: anaemia is mistakenly conflated with iron deficiency In India. The evidence is otherwise: in national Indian surveys, it has been shown that iron deficiency is not the major cause of anaemia. Indeed, fully one-third of anaemia cases demonstrate no micronutrient deficiency or obvious cause. Even so, giving iron should have sorted out those who did have iron deficiency anaemia, and reduced the general anaemia prevalence. While this could be a problem with inefficient programme implementation, two important questions arise: is there is really a deficiency in dietary iron intake in India? And is the administered iron being adequately absorbed and utilised for haemoglobin formation?

articles.title: Lam Research conducts finale of nationwide semiconductor challenge at PES college
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: More than 800 teams, each comprising four students from multidisciplinary backgrounds, from 190 colleges, including IITs and leading NIRF-ranked engineering institutions, competed in Lam’s advanced systems engineering challenge

Lam Research, a supplier of wafer fabrication equipment, has brought students from several top engineering institutions in India under the Lam Research Challenge 2026, the California-based firm’s annual advanced semiconductor systems competition.

More than 800 teams, each comprising four students from multidisciplinary backgrounds, from 190 colleges, including IITs and leading NIRF-ranked engineering institutions, competed in Lam’s advanced systems engineering challenge. The participation underscored the growing importance of systems engineering skills needed to design, build and optimise increasingly complex semiconductor manufacturing technologies.

Following a multi-stage, three-month competition that included qualification and hardware-build rounds, selected teams advanced to the finale. The winners were announced at the grand finale held at PES University in Bengaluru.
During the finale, participants developed solutions to complex technical challenges, demonstrating creativity, engineering execution and the ability to translate ideas into working outcomes.

According to Lam Research, entries were evaluated on innovation, technical excellence, collaboration, problem-solving and performance under pressure, with IIT Guwahati emerging as the overall winner. IIT Ropar finished runner-up and NIT Calicut second runner-up. The winners shared prize money worth ₹10 lakh, while select students were offered internship opportunities with Lam Research.

“Semiconductor manufacturing is one of the most sophisticated engineering environments in the world today, requiring talent that can solve complex, systems-level challenges,” said Rangesh Raghavan, Corporate Vice President and Managing Director, Lam Research India.
According to Mr. Raghavan, the Lam Research Challenge is designed to help students build capabilities while gaining exposure to the kinds of engineering problems shaping the future of the industry.

He said advanced semiconductor manufacturing requires expertise spanning hardware, software, automation, data science, process engineering and advanced controls, making systems engineering a critical capability for the industry’s future growth. Unlike traditional engineering competitions focused on individual disciplines, the Lam Research Challenge encourages participants to apply systems-level thinking and understand how multiple technologies and functions interact within large-scale manufacturing operations, the company said.

Mr. Raghavan said the industry’s talent requirements are evolving beyond traditional engineering disciplines. Modern semiconductor manufacturing environments require engineers who can understand and optimise entire systems rather than individual components in isolation, creating growing demand for talent capable of integrating technologies across increasingly complex engineering environments.

Building the pipeline of future talent continues to be important as India expands its role across semiconductor manufacturing, advanced packaging, equipment engineering and the broader electronics ecosystem, he added.

articles.title: Three Namma Metro Pink Line stations to be renamed
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Union Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs has approved the renaming of three stations on Bengaluru’s Namma Metro Pink Line following demands from local residents and elected representatives, according to Greater Bengaluru Authority Minister Krishna Byre Gowda and Bengaluru South Member of Parliament Tejasvi Surya.
Both said the changes were approved in response to public demands and on the recommendation of a committee of which Mr. Surya was a member.

Under the revised names, IIMB Metro Station will be renamed Bilekahalli–IIMB, JP Nagar 4th Phase will become N.S. Palya–J.P. Nagar 4th Phase, and Tavarekere will be renamed S.G. Palya (Suddagunte Palya).

The request was jointly submitted by elected representatives, including Forest, Ecology and Environment Minister Ramalinga Reddy, Mr. Gowda, Mr. Surya and MLAs Satish Reddy, Uday Garudachar and M. Krishnappa.

articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Indore, ranked the cleanest city in the country for the past eight years, did not figure among the winners this year
Navi Mumbai has been adjudged the cleanest city in India at a central government awards programme, while Gujarat’s Surat was second and Vijayawada in Andhra Pradesh finished third.
Among cities with a population between three lakh and 10 lakh, Madhya Pradesh’s Ujjain emerged as the cleanest urban centre, followed by the UT of Chandigarh and Guntur in Andhra Pradesh.
Indore, which had been ranked the cleanest city in the country for the past eight years, did not figure among the toppers this year.
The awards were presented by President Droupadi Murmu at an event held here.
Rewa, another city in Madhya Pradesh, emerged as the cleanest riverfront town, followed by Bilaspur (Chhattisgarh) and Varanasi (Uttar Pradesh) in second and third place, respectively.
In the 10 lakh-plus population category, Greater Visakhapatnam emerged as the cleanest city, followed by Jabalpur and Lucknow.
According to the Union Housing and Urban Affairs Ministry, in the Swachh Coastal Town category, Puri in Odisha was ranked first, followed by Kerala’s Alappuzha and Maharashtra’s Ratnagiri.
Rudrapur, in Uttarakhand, emerged as the cleanest Himalayan city, while Jammu secured the second position.
Last year, Indore had topped the league, followed by Surat and Navi Mumbai. Jaipur was recognised as the cleanest city in Rajasthan, while Gwalior received the distinction in Madhya Pradesh.

Swachh Survekshan is Swacch Bharat Mission-Urban’s flagship cleanliness assessment, with the goal of improving urban sanitation, hygiene, and waste management. Over 4,751 cities participated in the latest edition.

articles.title: Epic failures: on electoral roll, welfare
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: The electoral roll cannot be used to determine welfare beneficiaries

Union Panchayati Raj Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh’s statement that voter identity cards, with biometric authentication, will replace Aadhaar as the basis for identifying beneficiaries and making payments under his Ministry’s schemes runs contrary to existing laws and regulations. Essentially, the electoral roll, prepared in several States through the flawed Special Intensive Revision (SIR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI), will become the dataset to vet the identities of beneficiaries. This contradicts the Supreme Court’s May 27 judgment on the Bihar SIR and its observations while hearing petitions against West Bengal’s orders removing people deleted during the SIR from the Public Distribution System and the Annapurna Yojana. The Court held that the ECI may undertake only a “limited enquiry” into citizenship to decide who belongs on the electoral roll, and that “any action taken pursuant thereto is confined to electoral consequences alone”. The consequence of deletion from the rolls, it said, is “correspondingly limited” to a person’s place on the roll and their right to vote. The Court also called the EPIC “a derivative document, issued on the basis of inclusion in the electoral roll”, and held that relying on it to verify that very roll would defeat the exercise. It is ironic that Mr. Singh now wants this “derivative document” to be the determinant of welfare benefits.

Not every citizen is an eligible voter, and tying benefits to the electoral roll is illogical and also cruel. In West Bengal, lakhs were deleted from the rolls , many for dubious “logical discrepancies”. In the appeals heard for reinstatement, 93% resulted in the restoration of names by September 2026, pointing to massive pre-election disenfranchisement. The Court has stated that it is yet to adjudicate on the legality of the ECI’s “logical discrepancies” method. The SIR was designed by the ECI to restrict enrolment through stringent residency criteria; thus, itinerant voters had to prove their eligibility. The Opposition, civil society and even some of the BJP’s allies have objected to this, but the BJP refuses to acknowledge the SIR’s flaws. This is partly because it has benefited from disenfranchisement — as in West Bengal. But the Minister’s remarks suggest another reason. The BJP-led coalition sees the pruned electoral rolls as a way to limit welfare, especially at a time when growth in tax revenues has slowed because of the Centre’s policies. Inordinately delaying the Census, changing the procedure to appoint Election Commissioners, who then run an exercise that disenfranchises millions by design, and now, using the resultant rolls to decide who gets welfare, all cut at the heart of the painstakingly built constitutional welfare state. The sooner the Court decides the petitions against the SIR, and reiterates that its rolls cannot be used to curtail welfare, the better.

articles.title: Young and fast: on F1’s youngest champion
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: As F1’s youngest champion, Kimi Antonelli can attract a new generation of fans

Andrea Kimi Antonelli etched his name in motorsport history by becoming the youngest driver to win a Formula One World Championship . The 20-year-old has secured his maiden title with four races to spare after finishing third at the Mexico Grand Prix on Sunday. The Italian’s feat is remarkable, for he has claimed the crown in his sophomore campaign, becoming only the fifth driver in history to do so in the first or second season. Mercedes signed Antonelli for its junior driver programme when he was just 12. Since then, the Italian’s step towards F1 has been meticulously managed. After acing the F4 championships, Antonelli skipped one level to transition to F2. And when the opportunity arose to fill a seat vacated by seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff took a bold gamble by drafting in the youngster. Antonelli’s rookie campaign in 2025 was baptism by fire, and he was outclassed by teammate George Russell. For 2026, F1 ushered in drastic changes with new engine and aerodynamic regulations, dramatically altering the dynamics of the cars. Though conventional wisdom suggested that the experienced Russell would be the favourite, the Italian prodigy embraced the challenge astonishingly well. This was best exemplified by how he won five consecutive races starting from the second round of the season.

One of the hardest things in F1 is handling the nerves associated with protecting the lead, especially when it is the driver’s first attempt at a Championship bid. Antonelli, though, was incredibly consistent throughout the year, and hardly made any errors. Titles are often decided by how a driver minimises his losses on bad days, and Antonelli showed great temperament in this regard. At the same time, he was ruthless on the track and made decisive overtaking manoeuvres. The defining race was in Monza, Italy, in September, where Antonelli charged from 19th on the grid to win his home Grand Prix, finishing ahead of Russell who started second. It was a statement of intent, and strengthened his grip on the trophy. Drivers often raise their games following a world title, more so when success comes early in their career. Considering the giant leap Antonelli made to become F1’s first champion to be born in the 21st century, he will undoubtedly attract a new generation of fans. The charm of the sport lies in its iconic driver rivalries such as Ayrton Senna versus Alain Prost, and Michael Schumacher versus Mika Hakkinen. With four-time champion Max Verstappen widely considered the gold standard of the present era, Antonelli could well be the perfect candidate to battle the Dutchman in F1’s next great rivalry.

articles.title: Trump debacle: On the U.S. midterm election results
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Democrats must use their win to influence policy and improve lives

President Donald Trump faced the worst political setback of his current term in office after the Republican Party lost control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives in the mid-term election. Democrats not only won resoundingly in their traditional stronghold States, such as Colorado, Oregon and Illinois, and held onto important swing States, such as Georgia, Michigan and Virginia, but they also made historic inroads into “red states” such as Texas, Kansas and Iowa. While Mr. Trump fumed that Republicans would have performed better had his name been on the ballot, he also appeared to be resigned to the imminent reality of working with Democratic lawmakers over the remaining two years of his administration. Beyond the immediate impact on the future functioning of the federal government, this week’s “bluenami” has also brought sweeping changes at the State level: Democrats won a Senate seat in Texas for the first time in 37 years; Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won in Michigan , making him the first Muslim Senator in history ; Chris Pappas of New Hampshire became the first openly gay man to be elected to the Senate ; and Senate Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries will soon be the first African-American Speaker of the House.
Federal judge orders 14-day delay on any work beginning on Trump’s monumental arch

It is ironic that Mr. Trump alluded to his name not being on the ballot as the cause for the Republican collapse because, for many voters, the midterm election was indeed a referendum on the second Trump administration’s performance in office. The result has been an unambiguous thumbs-down from voters so far as top policy areas of the Trump administration are concerned, including cost of living and jobs, immigration enforcement, the war in Iran. The writing was on the wall, as were the approval ratings, especially in the case of oil prices and the Iran war, given that the price of gas in the U.S. has soared since the conflict around the Strait of Hormuz escalated. Similarly, the widespread raids by ICE and accelerated deportation processes for undocumented migrants led to protests across States and galvanised progressives around immigration reform. While Democrats may be justified in celebrating their victory after two years of harsh Trumpism, they would do well to remember that the President still retains a veto vote for policies passed by Congress. The temptation to launch a series of investigations and interrogate the functioning of the Trump White House may be strong, yet congressional Democrats may wish to avoid any posturing that yields no palpable policy impact, including kicking off impeachment proceedings against Mr. Trump. A more productive way forward for Democratic lawmakers would be to engage with the White House and, through negotiation and compromise, mitigate the real impact of deleterious policies in critical areas such as health-care insurance and tariffs.

🎯 Exam Relevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions

Democrats must use their win to influence policy and improve lives

President Donald Trump faced the worst political setback of his current term in office after the Republican Party lost control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives in the mid-term election. Democrats not only won resoundingly in their traditional stronghold States, such as Colorado, Oregon and Illinois, and held onto important swing States, such as Georgia, Michigan and Virginia, but they also made historic inroads into “red states” such as Texas, Kansas and Iowa. While Mr. Trump fumed that Republicans would have performed better had his name been on the ballot, he also appeared to be resigned to the imminent reality of working with Democratic lawmakers over the remaining two years of his administration. Beyond the immediate impact on the future functioning of the federal government, this week’s “bluenami” has also brought sweeping changes at the State level: Democrats won a Senate seat in Texas for the first time in 37 years; Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won in Michigan , making him the first Muslim Senator in history ; Chris Pappas of New Hampshire became the first openly gay man to be elected to the Senate ; and Senate Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries will soon be the first African-American Speaker of the House.

Federal judge orders 14-day delay on any work beginning on Trump’s monumental arch

It is ironic that Mr. Trump alluded to his name not being on the ballot as the cause for the Republican collapse because, for many voters, the midterm election was indeed a referendum on the second Trump administration’s performance in office. The result has been an unambiguous thumbs-down from voters so far as top policy areas of the Trump administration are concerned, including cost of living and jobs, immigration enforcement, the war in Iran. The writing was on the wall, as were the approval ratings, especially in the case of oil prices and the Iran war, given that the price of gas in the U.S. has soared since the conflict around the Strait of Hormuz escalated. Similarly, the widespread raids by ICE and accelerated deportation processes for undocumented migrants led to protests across States and galvanised progressives around immigration reform. While Democrats may be justified in celebrating their victory after two years of harsh Trumpism, they would do well to remember that the President still retains a veto vote for policies passed by Congress. The temptation to launch a series of investigations and interrogate the functioning of the Trump White House may be strong, yet congressional Democrats may wish to avoid any posturing that yields no palpable policy impact, including kicking off impeachment proceedings against Mr. Trump. A more productive way forward for Democratic lawmakers would be to engage with the White House and, through negotiation and compromise, mitigate the real impact of deleterious policies in critical areas such as health-care insurance and tariffs.

articles.title: Danger in the sewer: On India’s sewer cleaning deaths
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India must eliminate situations that lead to sewer cleaning deaths

Despite legislation, Supreme Court orders, government programmes, the availability of mechanised cleaning technologies, and exhortations from politicians, India continues to lose sanitation workers to foreseeable, and largely preventable, circumstances. In a recent incident, four workers lost their lives in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh , cleaning a hotel’s food-waste chamber. According to Parliament and the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis data, the number of workers who died on jobs involving sewer and septic tanks was 859 between 2014 and 2025, 498 from 2019 to mid-2026, 332 across 18 States and Union Territories in 2021-26, and 1,350 between 1993 and 2025. The figures have never tended towards zero even as the Safai Karamchari Andolan has repeatedly alleged severe under-reporting. Further, the government has maintained since at least 2021 that the practice of manually cleaning excreta from insanitary latrines has been eliminated, effectively signalling that it believes it has addressed the root of the problem when it has not, and freeing administrative bodies of the urgency of inspecting municipalities and private establishments. Members of historically marginalised castes are also overrepresented in these jobs. The law has distinguished hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks from manual scavenging since 2013. Even so, persons entering them are still vulnerable to noxious gases. In Dr. Balram Singh (2023), the Court strengthened the requirements under Safai Karamchari Andolan (2014) to, among other measures, ensure outsourced sewer-cleaning contracts did not entail workers entering sewers and raise the compensation for deaths to ₹30 lakh per worker. In 2025, there was an order to end manual sewer cleaning in four metropolitan cities, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad followed a year later with notices to 15 Chief Secretaries for disobeying the 2023 order, including on the compensation.

Private contractors and municipal bodies are known to violate the restrictions on manual cleaning specified in the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act 2013 and Rules, and evade liability by hiring undocumented daily-wage workers. The scourge of such worker deaths thus cannot be eliminated without also formalising their employment and improving social security across caste lines. A significant gap between aims and outcomes has also persisted under the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem scheme . And while it is centred on urban local bodies, its difficulties speak to the state’s fundamental error: to maximise administrative assistance, such as by distributing kits, rather than minimising the number of situations that could lead to worker deaths.

articles.title: Slow recovery: On the ISRO’s GSLV-F18 mission
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: ISRO needs more human and material resources to fulfil its mandate

With the successful launch of the GSLV-F18 mission and the NVS-03 satellite’s healthy status , the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is on course to heave a sigh of relief. Its last 18 months have been constrained by the consequences of two launch failures involving PSLV rockets , which share some of their design aspects with GSLV, to the extent that the F18 mission was only the second successful launch of 2026. If the NVS-03 satellite is successfully manoeuvred into its final intended orbital slot and commissioned, ISRO will also have pulled off a rescue mission for the ‘Navigation with Indian Constellation’ (NavIC) programme , which has been at least one functional satellite short for the last six months and thus unable to meet its primary purpose of providing standalone positioning services over the Indian subcontinent. The three second-generation NVS satellites thus far are distinguished by having at least one indigenously made atomic clock onboard, in line with the recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee (PSC) on Science and Technology and India’s investments in quantum timekeeping, and away from the imported clocks onboard the first-generation IRNSS satellites.

The PSC had also flagged procurement bottlenecks across ISRO’s programmes, including difficulties with obtaining specialised components and ensuring vendor readiness on the timelines that NavIC needs. The ISRO Space Applications Centre’s ‘request for proposals’ in 2025 also specified a large lead time of nearly two years between a contract’s start and the first two flight models. The Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme and the programme to modernise the Semiconductor Laboratory can be tweaked to serve these needs, with the Electronics Ministry also setting aside dedicated funds for developing specialised components and their qualification tests in a five- to seven-year programme. In tandem, the government must allocate around ₹17,000 crore in the 2027-28 Union Budget for the Department of Space, against ₹13,705.6 crore in 2026-27, with the hike focusing on manufacturing launch vehicles, replacing satellites, and recruitment. Besides, NavIC also requires a dedicated operator, so that ISRO can be left to focus on its core mandate, and India needs a national space law addressing private participation in this enterprise, and liability. Two successful orbital missions in five-sixths of a year is unbecoming of a national space programme with imminent plans of human spaceflight, a space station, and reusable launch vehicle capabilities. Without significant measures, ISRO will lurch from one mission to the next as and when its inadequate workforce is able to make do with its inadequate allocation.

✍️ Editorial & Opinion 📅 10 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

📰 Slow recovery: On the ISRO’s GSLV-F18 mission

🎯 Exam Relevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
