Tuberculosis remains a major public health challenge, as treatment requires a combination of antibiotics taken over several months and is becoming increasingly difficult due to the emergence of resistant strains

A team of scientists at the CSIR-Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CCMB) has identified critical weaknesses in the bacterium that causes Tuberculosis (TB), a finding that could pave the way for the development of new treatments against one of the world’s deadliest infectious diseases.

The discovery is particularly significant for India, which accounts for nearly a quarter of global TB cases and about a third of drug-resistant infections, according to the World Health Organisation’s Global TB Report 2025 . Drug-resistant TB remains a major public health challenge, as treatment requires a combination of antibiotics taken over several months and is becoming increasingly difficult due to the emergence of resistant strains.

Led by CCMB Director Vinay Kumar Nandicoori, the research team mapped the protein export machinery of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), the bacterium responsible for TB. The study sheds light on how the pathogen transports proteins within and outside its cells, a process essential for its growth, survival and ability to cause disease.

The research was carried out by joint first authors Priyadarshini Sanyal and Jagadeeshwari Uppada in collaboration with scientists from the Institute of Mathematical Sciences, Chennai, led by Areejit Samal, and the Translational Health Science and Technology Institute, Faridabad.

Using a combination of computational modelling and laboratory experiments, the researchers identified 92 key components and nearly 200 molecular reactions involved in the bacterium’s protein transport network. These included the general Sec pathway, the Twin-Arginine Translocation (Tat) system and the specialised ESX secretion systems unique to this group of bacteria.

“Protein secretion acts like a delivery system inside the bacterium and is vital for its survival,” said Dr Uppada. The team focused on two major secretion pathways, SecA1 and Tat, employing CRISPR-based gene-silencing technology to reduce their activity. The results were striking: bacterial growth declined sharply both in laboratory cultures and inside immune cells, demonstrating that both pathways are essential for the pathogen’s survival.

Dr Priyadarshini Sanyal said further analysis revealed that disrupting these systems affected the export of more than 100 proteins in the SecA1 pathway and around 140 proteins linked to the Tat system. Researchers also observed structural damage to the bacterial cell membrane, making it unstable and more permeable. Proteins that normally remain inside the bacterium began leaking into the surrounding environment.

Dr Nandicoori said that these changes highlight the close connection between protein secretion and the maintenance of the bacterial cell envelope, a key factor behind TB’s persistence and resistance to treatment. The findings, published in the peer-reviewed journal Molecular & Cellular Proteomics , could help researchers identify new drug targets, although translating the discovery into effective medicines will require several more years of research.

articles.title: Nvidia, CEO Huang sued over disclosures related to suspected Chinese spy
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Jensen Huang told Nvidia's employees he had ⁠been unfaithful to his wife, without disclosing details of the alleged relationship

Nvidia ​and Chief Executive Jensen Huang were sued on ‌Monday (November 9, 2026) in a proposed class action accusing ​them of defrauding shareholders by ⁠concealing Huang's ties with a suspected Chinese spy.

According to a complaint filed in federal court ‌in San Jose, California, the defendants misled shareholders about Huang's alleged affair with ‌Alice Huang, a former executive ‌of Singapore-based ⁠Megaspeed who is not related to ⁠him, and did not disclose that the matter raised national security concerns that threatened Nvidia's reputation and ​business prospects.
The New ‌York Times reported last month about the alleged relationship, and that U.S. authorities had concluded Alice Huang was a Chinese intelligence ‌asset.
Nvidia did not immediately respond to ​a request for comment.
Jensen Huang told Nvidia's employees he had ⁠been unfaithful to his wife, without disclosing details of the alleged relationship.

He co-founded Nvidia and ‌has led the Santa Clara, California-based company as it became the world's most valuable chipmaker and made him one of the world's most prominent symbols of the artificial intelligence boom.

Nvidia announced a probe into ‌the matter on Sunday (November 8, 2026). Its shares closed down ​4.3% on Monday (November 9, 2026), reducing Nvidia's market capitalisation by approximately $190 billion. The lawsuit ⁠was filed five minutes after the U.S. stock ⁠market closed.
It is common for shareholders to sue companies after unexpected share ‌price declines. Nvidia shareholders, led by Mark Kistenmacher are seeking unspecified damages from ​the defendants.

articles.title: Judge sets summer 2028 trial for the man accused of killing Charlie Kirk
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Utah District Judge Graf allocated 105 days for the trial, beginning with jury selection on June 21, 2028
The man accused of assassinating conservative activist Charlie Kirk will stand trial in the summer of 2028, a Utah judge ruled on Monday (November 9, 2026).

Attorneys for defendant Tyler Robinson, 23, proposed a trial starting in 2029. But District Judge Tony Graf faced pressure from Kirk's family and supporters , including President Donald Trump, to speed up court proceedings that already have lasted more than a year.

Robinson has pleaded not guilty to aggravated murder in the killing of Kirk, 31, as the activist spoke to several thousand people at Utah Valley University on September 10, 2025 . Robinson could face the death penalty if convicted.

District Judge Graf allocated 105 days for the trial, beginning with jury selection on June 21, 2028. He said the dates balance Robinson's right to prepare his defense with the rights of Kirk's widow, Erika Kirk, to a speedy resolution.
Erika Kirk's attorney disagreed with the schedule but said there is no choice but to accept it.

“A trial in the summer of 2028, three years after Charlie's assassination, does not feel very speedy to the Kirk family,” attorney Jeffrey Neiman told the judge. He had argued the trial should start next October.

In a statement after Monday's (November 9, 2026) hearing, the Kirk family characterised District Judge Graf's decision as a “delay” and said, “every additional day without justice prolongs our family's pain.”
Robinson's defense team declined to comment after the hearing.
The defendant turned himself in a day after the shooting. His lawyers have not offered alternative theories for Kirk's death.
Prosecutors had said they could be ready for trial by October 2027. Rather than hold the proceedings during the Thanksgiving and Christmas holidays, they proposed a January 2028 start date.

Robinson's defense team declined to comment after the hearing.

The defendant turned himself in a day after the shooting. His lawyers have not offered alternative theories for Kirk's death.

Prosecutors had said they could be ready for trial by October 2027. Rather than hold the proceedings during the Thanksgiving and Christmas holidays, they proposed a January 2028 start date.

The stock market debut is being seen as a gauge of how long the AI spending boom lifting the US economy can last.

articles.title: Award-winning Keralam farmer who used his banana farming as cover for smuggling drugs arrested
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Dhanesh S. Nair had allegedly trained members of his drug network on how to conceal drugs inside banana bunches
The Ernakulam Rural police have arrested an award-winning 31-year-old farmer suspected to be running a drug network under the cover of his agriculture ventures.

Dhanesh S. Nair, aka Dani, of Haripad, Alappuzha district was arrested with 803 grams of suspected hashish oil and 8 grams of suspected MDMA, the police said on Monday (November 9, 2026). The investigating team zeroed in on the accused as part of the probe into the recent arrest of Harikrishnan K.S., 32, of Palluruthy, Kochi with 185 gram of suspected MDMA from a lodge in Aluva.

The accused, who lives near Nanjanagudu, Mysuru, was nabbed by a special investigation team, led by District Police Chief (Ernakulam Rural) K.S. Sudarshan when he landed in Angamaly. The police suspect he was engaged in drug peddling under the cover of banana cultivation in Nanjanagudu.

He had reportedly pursued a higher education programme in Agribusiness in Germany between 2015 and 2018. He later returned to Keralam during the floods in 2018 and ventured into farming. The police said he had won a government award for the best young farmer in Haripad in 2022.

He had allegedly trained members of his network on how to conceal drugs inside banana bunches. Videos of the accused showing them methods to conceal drugs inside banana bunches were allegedly recovered from his mobile phone. The banana bunches were transported to Keralam under the guise of carrying agricultural produce. He had reportedly recruited youth to transport and distribute the drugs in Bengaluru and nearby areas. The drugs were later brought to Keralam and distributed among local suppliers and consumers.

Earlier, the police had held Shinu Sebastian, 34, of Thoppumpady with seven gram of suspected MDMA following the arrest of Mr. Harikrishnan. The police, sources said, suspect Mr. Harikrishnan and Mr. Sebastian were engaged in alleged drug peddling as per instructions given by Mr. Nair through social media.

articles.title: Supreme Court goes beyond Deepavali AQI, flags vehicular emissions polluting Delhi air
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The court says Delhi and the NCR bear the ‘cumulative burden of vehicular traffic’ and seeks to know what has been done to regulate in the capital the entry and plying of vehicles from neighbouring States

Forty-eight hours before Deepavali, amidst the rising crescendo of crackers heralding the festivities, a Supreme Court Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said the people, and not the judiciary, must strike a blow against air pollution in the national capital.

Instead, the court went beyond Deepavali to highlight a consistent danger that sustains and would worsen the toxic air: vehicular emissions. On November 6, the court detected a sharp increase in issues attributable to vehicular emissions.

It told the authorities that the thick smog, which later raised the city’s Air Quality Index (AQI) to almost the ‘severe’ category following Deepavali, had nowhere to go in the landlocked capital. The substantial commercial and non-commercial traffic entering Delhi would only compound the problem in the coming days.

“It must be borne in mind that Delhi and the National Capital Region (NCR), by virtue of their geographical and economic interconnectedness, bear the cumulative burden of vehicular traffic originating not merely within their own boundaries but also from the neighbouring States of Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Rajasthan,” the Supreme Court reminded the authorities in its latest order.

The issue warranted urgent and immediate intervention, the court said, directing the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD), the Delhi government, the Delhi Police (Traffic department), as well as the neighbouring States of Haryana, Rajasthan, and Uttar Pradesh to file their responses on what they have done to regulate in the national capital the entry and plying of commercial and non-commercial vehicles.

The court wanted to know about measures to regulate traffic originating from outside the national capital. These include steps taken to identify, monitor, and regulate vehicles that do not conform to prescribed emission standards, and measures to prevent the entry and operation of overage, end-of-life, or non-compliant vehicles.

The Bench has specifically sought information on the measures undertaken against violations, including the number of vehicles inspected, challaned, denied entry, and the coordination mechanisms between the authorities of Delhi and the neighbouring States for regulating inter-State vehicular movement.

The court has asked if the authorities have any “further short-term and long-term measures proposed or contemplated to mitigate vehicular emissions and reduce their contribution to the deteriorating air quality in Delhi and the National Capital Region”.

Incidentally, two separate orders of the Supreme Court passed several months ago, on January 21 and February 23 this year, had contained detailed long-term and short-term measures recommended by the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) to mitigate air pollution, especially caused by vehicular emissions, in Delhi.

The January 21 order had listed various CAQM recommendations, including phasing out polluting vehicles from Delhi-NCR, fortifying the pollution-under-check regime, augmentation of rail transport and metro models, revised electric vehicle policy, among others.

articles.title: Keralam CPI(M) awaits ICC report on complaint against former Palakkad secretary
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Complainant had made allegations of sexual misconduct against Babu; party State leadership to decide on further action based on findings in report

The Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] has stepped up its internal inquiry into a sexual misconduct complaint against former Palakkad district secretary E.N. Suresh Babu. The party’s internal complaints committee (ICC) is investigating the complaint. It has reportedly completed key procedures, including recording the statement of the woman who filed the complaint.
The complainant is a lawyer and a party leader. She is understood to have submitted digital evidence in support of her allegations against Mr. Babu.

The ICC will submit its inquiry report and recommendations to the CPI(M) State committee after completing the investigation. The State leadership will decide on further action against Mr. Babu based on the findings. The possibility of disciplinary action, including removal from primary membership, is also being discussed within the party.

As per the party’s rules, a complaint against a leader of an organisational unit must be investigated by the ICC of the next higher committee. Since Mr. Babu was the Palakkad district secretary when the complaint was raised, the matter was referred to the ICC under the party central committee.

The woman’s complaint had earlier led to the intervention of the State leadership and Mr. Babu’s removal from the district secretary post. On October 4, the party appointed former MLA V. Chenthamarakshan as his successor at an extended district committee meeting. The CPI(M) had officially described the change as part of its organisational review following the electoral setback.

The party had maintained that Mr. Babu stepped down voluntarily due to personal reasons, denying any link between his removal and the complaint. However, the ICC inquiry has brought the circumstances surrounding his exit as district secretary back into focus.
The complaint reportedly relates to an incident at the CPI(M) district committee office in Palakkad, where the woman had been called.

The issue is likely to come up for further discussion at the State leadership level after the ICC submits its report. The findings and recommendations will determine the next course of action against Mr. Babu.

articles.title: Oxford University returns remains of 39 Naga people after more than a century
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The remains were formally handed over to the Forum for Naga Reconciliation and the Naga Tribe Hoho at a ceremony held at the museum on November 9, 2026
The University of Oxford returned the remains of 39 members of the Naga community, which were held at its Pitt Rivers Museum for more than a century, in a historic repatriation initiative.
The remains were formally handed over to the Forum for Naga Reconciliation (FNR) and the Naga Tribe Hoho at a ceremony held at the museum on Monday (November 9, 2026).

The transfer of title document was signed by Pitt Rivers Museum Director Professor Laura Van Broekhoven and FNR representative Rev. Dr. Wati Aier. It was witnessed by Visier Sanyu on behalf of the FNR and Thejao Vihienuo representing the Naga Tribe Hoho.
Following the handover, the ancestral remains were moved from the University of Oxford to begin their journey to Nagaland, according to a statement issued by the FNR on Tuesday (November 10, 2026).

The remains had been part of the collections of the Pitt Rivers Museum, established in 1884, which houses cultural artefacts collected from various parts of the world. Addressing the ceremony, University of Oxford Vice-Chancellor Professor Irene Tracey described the handover as a historic moment in the relationship between the university and the Naga people.
“She said the initiative reflected a community-led effort towards reconciliation, healing and peace,” the statement said.

Mr. Sanyu spoke about the impact of British colonial violence on Naga communities and recounted how his own village was burnt by colonial forces. Emphasising the importance of forgiveness and reconciliation, he quoted late Naga peace activist Niketu Iralu as saying, "Hate not transformed is transferred".

Thejao Vihienuo, president of the Angami Public Organisation, who represented the Naga Tribe Hoho, said the return of the ancestral remains was the right of the Naga people to care for their ancestors. He called for the return of all Naga ancestral remains held in museums to their homeland with dignity.
Meanwhile, preparations have begun for the burial of the remains at Naga Solidarity Park in Kohima. The Naga Solidarity Park Management Committee has allocated a designated site within the park.
A prayer service was recently held at the park to mark the formal commencement of preparatory work for the proposed burial site, the committee's convenor Vipopal Kintsi said.

The remains were formally handed over to the Forum for Naga Reconciliation and the Naga Tribe Hoho at a ceremony held at the museum on November 9, 2026

The University of Oxford returned the remains of 39 members of the Naga community, which were held at its Pitt Rivers Museum for more than a century, in a historic repatriation initiative.

The remains were formally handed over to the Forum for Naga Reconciliation (FNR) and the Naga Tribe Hoho at a ceremony held at the museum on Monday (November 9, 2026).

The transfer of title document was signed by Pitt Rivers Museum Director Professor Laura Van Broekhoven and FNR representative Rev. Dr. Wati Aier. It was witnessed by Visier Sanyu on behalf of the FNR and Thejao Vihienuo representing the Naga Tribe Hoho.

Following the handover, the ancestral remains were moved from the University of Oxford to begin their journey to Nagaland, according to a statement issued by the FNR on Tuesday (November 10, 2026).

The remains had been part of the collections of the Pitt Rivers Museum, established in 1884, which houses cultural artefacts collected from various parts of the world. Addressing the ceremony, University of Oxford Vice-Chancellor Professor Irene Tracey described the handover as a historic moment in the relationship between the university and the Naga people.

“She said the initiative reflected a community-led effort towards reconciliation, healing and peace,” the statement said.

Mr. Sanyu spoke about the impact of British colonial violence on Naga communities and recounted how his own village was burnt by colonial forces. Emphasising the importance of forgiveness and reconciliation, he quoted late Naga peace activist Niketu Iralu as saying, "Hate not transformed is transferred".

Thejao Vihienuo, president of the Angami Public Organisation, who represented the Naga Tribe Hoho, said the return of the ancestral remains was the right of the Naga people to care for their ancestors. He called for the return of all Naga ancestral remains held in museums to their homeland with dignity.

Meanwhile, preparations have begun for the burial of the remains at Naga Solidarity Park in Kohima. The Naga Solidarity Park Management Committee has allocated a designated site within the park.

A prayer service was recently held at the park to mark the formal commencement of preparatory work for the proposed burial site, the committee's convenor Vipopal Kintsi said.

articles.title: Former DMK Minister Anbil Mahesh’s bail plea dismissed in alleged multi-crore private school bribery case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Anbil Mahesh was arrested on October 26 and remanded in judicial custody till November 18

A special court on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) dismissed the bail petition filed by former Tamil Nadu School Education Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi, who is accused of receiving a share of an alleged multi-crore bribe collected from private school managements allegedly through threats, deception, and false promises of securing government approvals.

D.C. Elangovan, secretary of the Private School Management Association, lodged a complaint with the Chennai Commissioner of Police on June 23, 2026, alleging that nearly ₹100 crore had been collected from private school managements through intimidation and forgery.

The complaint named B.T. Arasakumar (Accused 1), who allegedly floated an unregistered body called the Tamil Nadu Private Schools Association (TNPSA), claiming to be its founder-president, and Muthukumar (Accused 2), a former MLA from Virudhachalam, as the key persons involved in the collection of bribes.

The two allegedly organised an event of the TNPSA at Kalaivanar Arangam in Chennai on December 30, 2024, which Mr. Poyyamozhi attended as the chief guest. The prosecution alleged that a bank account was subsequently opened in the name of BTK Educational Development Trust at the Canara Bank’s Tondiarpet branch; this account was used to collect membership fees and other amounts from private schools.

The FIR alleged that the accused assured school managements that they could obtain government approvals and permissions easily, even if their institutions lacked basic requirements. They allegedly threatened that schools refusing to pay the demanded amounts would not receive the necessary permissions, potentially affecting students appearing for the SSLC and Class XII public examinations.

Dismissing the bail petition, Special Court Judge L.S. Sathiyamurthy noted that statements from witnesses, including private school correspondents and managers, had been recorded by the investigating officer and before the Judicial Magistrate. “A preliminary examination of these statements indicated a prima facie link between the petitioner and the alleged offence,” the judge observed.

The investigating agency had also seized computers and other digital devices from Mr. Poyyamozhi’s premises and sent them to a forensic laboratory for examination. The court said it would have to await the findings of the cyber forensic experts.

Observing that the investigation was still at an early stage and the first period of remand had only just concluded, the Special Court Judge said the materials collected so far indicated that substantial sums had been extorted from multiple private school managements through deception and threats. Witness statements suggested that money collected by A1, A2, and their associates had reached the petitioner under the guise of a ‘party fund’, it said.

Classifying the case as a multi-crore economic offence involving several victims, the court pointed out that some of the accused were yet to be arrested and the custodial interrogation of Muthukumar who had surrendered after the arrest of Mr. Poyyamozhi and other accused, was at an initial stage.

The court also underscored the responsibility attached to public office, observing that the petitioner, as School Education Minister, had been entrusted with the welfare of students, teachers, and parents.

articles.title: Industry seeks LTCG, STT cuts in Budget 2027; MSME relief also on wish list
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Several industry bodies have been meeting top officials of the Finance Ministry as part of the annual pre-Budget consultation process

Several industry bodies have recommended to the Ministry of Finance that the upcoming Budget 2027 should rationalise the Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) tax rate on equities and reduce the rate of the Securities Transaction Tax (STT).

Officials in the Finance Ministry, including Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and Revenue Secretary Arvind Shrivastava, have been conducting their pre-Budget consultative meetings, during which they met the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI), the PHD Chamber of Commerce and Industry (PHDCCI), and the Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industry (ASSOCHAM), among others.

One of the most-cited requests from the industry was the rationalisation of LTCG on equities. In Budget 2026, the Centre removed the 12.5% LTCG tax in the government securities market for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) alongside other measures including reforms under the Fully Accessible Route (FAR).

Currently, foreign and domestic investors have to pay 12.5% tax on the sale of equities on gains exceeding Rs 1.25 lakh per annum on listed shares. The Centre has held several meetings with the Securities and Exchange Board of India, the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) and other industry players.

“Removing the LTCG levy would raise post-tax returns and close a gap with Korea, Taiwan and Brazil,” Rakesh Nangia, chairman of task force on International Taxes at ASSOCHAM said. “The debt market is a useful precedent, which after the G-sec relief, saw FPI inflows rise to about $9 billion in June-July.”

The PHDCCI has requested that the government abolish LTCG tax on equity investments, reduce the short-term capital gains (STCG) tax rate from 20% to 10%, and lower STT rates “to encourage long-term investment and improve India’s capital market competitiveness”.

In its representation to Ms. Sitharaman, FICCI highlighted the fact that foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have withdrawn about Rs 3.08 lakh crore during the year. It added that capital gains tax, which is charged over and above the STT, erodes returns from equities, and needs a review to make India a more attractive place to invest.

However, other market players highlight that the revenue loss incurred from the removal of LTCG could be negated through a hike in STT. According to estimates by SBI Research, the removal of LTCG would result in a revenue loss of Rs 40,000-50,000 crore for FY28.

One of the key frictions for FPIs underscored by industry bodies and equity analysts is the computation of the tax. Under Income-Tax Act, the calculation of the LTCG is in the Indian rupee. The challenge arises due to currency depreciation as against the investor’s base currency during the holding period, due to which investors are still liable to pay tax even when net returns in dollar terms are flat or even negative. This issue is currently under examination.

VK Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist at Geojit Financial Services also cautioned against selective relief, noting that abolishing LTCG solely for FPIs would be discriminatory against domestic retail and direct equity investors who remain subject to the 12.5% tax. He urged any tax relief must apply equally across the board to ensure a level playing field.

📈 Economic, Banking & Finance 📅 10 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 4 Min Read

📰 Industry seeks LTCG, STT cuts in Budget 2027; MSME relief also on wish list

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

Several industry bodies have been meeting top officials of the Finance Ministry as part of the annual pre-Budget consultation process

Several industry bodies have recommended to the Ministry of Finance that the upcoming Budget 2027 should rationalise the Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) tax rate on equities and reduce the rate of the Securities Transaction Tax (STT).

Officials in the Finance Ministry, including Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and Revenue Secretary Arvind Shrivastava, have been conducting their pre-Budget consultative meetings, during which they met the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI), the PHD Chamber of Commerce and Industry (PHDCCI), and the Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industry (ASSOCHAM), among others.

One of the most-cited requests from the industry was the rationalisation of LTCG on equities. In Budget 2026, the Centre removed the 12.5% LTCG tax in the government securities market for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) alongside other measures including reforms under the Fully Accessible Route (FAR).

Currently, foreign and domestic investors have to pay 12.5% tax on the sale of equities on gains exceeding Rs 1.25 lakh per annum on listed shares. The Centre has held several meetings with the Securities and Exchange Board of India, the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) and other industry players.

“Removing the LTCG levy would raise post-tax returns and close a gap with Korea, Taiwan and Brazil,” Rakesh Nangia, chairman of task force on International Taxes at ASSOCHAM said. “The debt market is a useful precedent, which after the G-sec relief, saw FPI inflows rise to about $9 billion in June-July.”

The PHDCCI has requested that the government abolish LTCG tax on equity investments, reduce the short-term capital gains (STCG) tax rate from 20% to 10%, and lower STT rates “to encourage long-term investment and improve India’s capital market competitiveness”.

In its representation to Ms. Sitharaman, FICCI highlighted the fact that foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have withdrawn about Rs 3.08 lakh crore during the year. It added that capital gains tax, which is charged over and above the STT, erodes returns from equities, and needs a review to make India a more attractive place to invest.

However, other market players highlight that the revenue loss incurred from the removal of LTCG could be negated through a hike in STT. According to estimates by SBI Research, the removal of LTCG would result in a revenue loss of Rs 40,000-50,000 crore for FY28.

One of the key frictions for FPIs underscored by industry bodies and equity analysts is the computation of the tax. Under Income-Tax Act, the calculation of the LTCG is in the Indian rupee. The challenge arises due to currency depreciation as against the investor’s base currency during the holding period, due to which investors are still liable to pay tax even when net returns in dollar terms are flat or even negative. This issue is currently under examination.

VK Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist at Geojit Financial Services also cautioned against selective relief, noting that abolishing LTCG solely for FPIs would be discriminatory against domestic retail and direct equity investors who remain subject to the 12.5% tax. He urged any tax relief must apply equally across the board to ensure a level playing field.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: VK Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist at Geojit Financial Services also cautioned against selective relief, noting that abolishing LTCG solely for FPIs would be discriminatory against domestic retail and direct equity investors who remain subject to the 12.5% tax. articles.title: Strait of Hormuz LNG traffic hits highest in October since Iran war began
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: October exports ‌were ⁠the highest since February when the war ⁠started and were up from September’s corresponding tally of 23 vessels exiting the strait

The monthly tally of laden liquefied natural gas (LNG) tankers exiting the ​Strait of Hormuz reached its highest in October since ‌the U.S.-Iran conflict disrupted shipping this year, vessel ​tracking data showed.

* Last month, ⁠31 LNG tankers went through the key waterway, according to data from S&P Global Energy, of which ‌23 were loaded at Ras Laffan in Qatar and eight at Das Island ‌in the United Arab Emirates.
* October exports ‌were ⁠the highest since February when the war ⁠started and were up from September’s corresponding tally of 23 vessels exiting the strait, the data showed.
* “We are ​looking at UAE ‌back to pre-war transit levels and Qatar at over 30% of pre-war Hormuz transits,” said Eric Yep, a senior principal analyst at ‌S&P Global Energy.
* Kpler’s shiptracking data showed ​42 LNG cargoes were loaded in October, up from 27 in September.

* ⁠The changes come as Ras Laffan’s October loadings reached 35 cargoes, surpassing 2.7 million tons, the ‌highest since the war started, according to Kpler data. Qatar exported nearly 6.2 million tons in February.

* Two of the vessels carrying LNG from Ras Laffan that exited the strait subsequently conducted ship-to-ship (STS) transfers off the coast of ‌Oman’s Sohar anchorage, Kpler data showed. The SC Prestige ​transferred LNG to the BW ENN Crystal Sky, which is now bound for ⁠South Korea.
* The Al Mafyar moved its LNG ⁠to Shandong Redwood and Ejnan, both of which delivered the cargoes to Pakistan.
* ‌Das Island exports held steady at seven loadings in October, flat with September, Kpler ​data showed.

articles.title: Malaysian court clears final hurdle for former PM Najib Razak's transfer to house arrest
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: “A High Court in Malaysia on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) cleared all legal hurdles for the transfer of imprisoned former Prime Minister Najib Razak to his home to serve the remainder of his graft sentence under house arrest,” his lawyer said.
Najib has been behind bars since August 2022, when the Kuala Lumpur High Court upheld his graft conviction linked to a multibillion-dollar looting of the state investment fund 1MDB.
In September, Najib was granted royal clemency, allowing him to serve the rest of his sentence under house arrest once he pays a court-imposed fine.

Last Friday, he left prison after his political party paid the 50 million ringgit ($12.3 million) fine but he was brought back hours later after the attorney general blocked the transfer, seeking legal clarifications.

The attorney general's request sparked a public rebuke from the palace, which said that King Sultan Ibrahim Iskandar's prerogative of pardon for Najib that allowed the house arrest was clear and must be respected. It said any attempts to challenge it would amount to defying the royal order.

Najib's lawyer Muhammad Shafee Abdullah said on Tuesday all was settled for the former Prime Minister's transfer to house arrest at his Kuala Lumpur home, where he is to remain until Aug 23, 2028. Najib appeared in court on Tuesday (November 10, 2026); the transfer was expected to take place later in the day. Police later sealed off the road leading to his home. “It's a final relief, you know, great sigh to him because he has been waiting for this,” the lawyer said.

The house arrest covers only Najib's reduced, six-year sentence in his first trial for graft and not a separate, 15-year sentence handed down last December for corruption and money laundering. That sentence followed a second major trial tied to the 1MDB scandal.
Najib is also appealing that sentence, which he is to serve after the end of his first sentence. If his appeal fails, he could return to prison after his house arrest ends.

Najib, who served as Prime Minister from 2009 to 2018, has denied any wrongdoing. He is Malaysia's first former leader to be imprisoned under a sentence related to the 1MDB scandal. It marked one of the world's largest financial scandals, rippling across global markets and triggering investigations in the United States and other countries.

articles.title: Pannun’s civil lawsuit: U.S. State Department formally serves notice on India
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The U.S. Department of State said it was legally obliged to do so and is not taking a position on the case

The U.S. State Department, through a diplomatic note, has formally served notice on the Government of India regarding Khalistan separatist Gurpatwant Pannun ’s civil lawsuit over an alleged assassination plot.

The U.S. State Department said it was legally obliged to do so and is not taking a position on the case, adding, “The documents were delivered to the Embassy of India in Washington under cover of the U.S. Department of State note dated October 20, 2026. The diplomatic note was signed on September 30, 2026, and delivered on October 9, 2026.”

The U.S. State Department’s diplomatic note said “I, John Ballard Managing Director of the Directorate of Overseas Citizens Services, in Washington certify that this is a true copy of the United States Department of State diplomatic note signed on September 30, 2026 and delivered to the Embassy of the Republic of India in Washington DC on October 9, 2026.”

On February 16, 2026, Indian citizen Nikhil Gupta had pled “guilty” at a court in New York to charges of murder, conspiracy, and money laundering to assassinate Khalistani activist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun. The government is yet to comment on the case.

According to investigators in the United States, Mr. Gupta , an Indian businessman, worked with an Indian “government employee” Vikash Yadav, believed to have been associated with India’s external intelligence agency R&AW, to hire a hitman to carry out Mr. Pannun’s murder for a total sum of $100,000. Mr. Yadav, who was arrested in December 2023 in Delhi in a separate case of kidnapping and extortion, has been out on bail since April 2024.

The MEA, responding to Pannun serving Doval, said, “We reject the fabricated and malicious attacks on our high officials, as also we reject the frivolous lawsuits. Request for serving of judicial documents in India can only be routed through India’s designated central authority, that is the Ministry of Law and Justice.”

articles.title: Poland arrests two Ukrainians over alleged Russian espionage, sabotage

fullParagraphs: Poland has long ⁠accused Russia and its ally Belarus of waging a hybrid campaign involving sabotage, cyberattacks ‌and disinformation since Moscow’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine
Poland has arrested two Ukrainian men suspected of espionage ​and sabotage on behalf of Russian intelligence ‌services, the Internal Security Agency (ABW) ​said on Tuesday (November 10, 2026).

Poland has long ⁠accused Russia and its ally Belarus of waging a hybrid campaign involving sabotage, cyberattacks ‌and disinformation since Moscow’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine. Russia has repeatedly ‌denied the accusations.

“According to findings ‌by ⁠the ABW, the suspects carried ⁠out tasks on behalf of Russian special services, which included, among other things, reconnoitring critical infrastructure ​and military facilities ‌throughout the country,” the agency said in a statement.

“The prosecutor has charged both detainees with engaging in espionage activities ‌on behalf of a foreign ​intelligence service against the Republic of Poland, as well as ⁠committing acts of sabotage.”

According to investigators, the men set fire to vehicles after replacing ‌their licence plates with ones resembling those used by the Ukrainian military. The men were paid for carrying out the tasks, including in cryptocurrencies.

“The investigation has established that the ‌acts of sabotage were carried out at the ​behest of Russian intelligence services and were intended to fuel anti-Ukrainian ⁠sentiment,” prosecutors said in a separate statement.
Both ⁠face from 10 years to life imprisonment if found guilty.
The Russian ‌embassy in Warsaw did not immediately respond to an emailed request ​for comment.

According to investigators, the men set fire to vehicles after replacing ‌their licence plates with ones resembling those used by the Ukrainian military. The men were paid for carrying out the tasks, including in cryptocurrencies.

“The investigation has established that the ‌acts of sabotage were carried out at the ​behest of Russian intelligence services and were intended to fuel anti-Ukrainian ⁠sentiment,” prosecutors said in a separate statement.

Both ⁠face from 10 years to life imprisonment if found guilty.

The Russian ‌embassy in Warsaw did not immediately respond to an emailed request ​for comment.

fullParagraphs: In her time, Kadambini Ganguly challenged convention to become the first Indian female doctor to practice Western medicine

Have you heard of the names Kadambini Ganguly and Anandibai Joshi? Considered India’s first female doctors, these names have often been looked past in the pages of history and even medical textbooks. Today, let’s talk about the story of Kadambini Ganguly — India’s first practising lady doctor.

It was in 1861 that Brahmo reformer and headmaster Braja Kishore Basu had a daughter. She was named Kadambini Basu. Young Kadambini, despite hailing from a community that did not necessarily support women’s education like many others at the time did, received an education at the Brahmo Eden Female School and later at the Hindu Mahila Vidyalaya.

As the daughter of someone who organised and fought for women’s emancipation, Kadambini went on to study in college and became the first woman to pass the University of Calcutta entrance examination. In 1882, she passed the examination for the Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree along with Chandramukhi Basu from the University of Calcutta, making her and Chandramukhi the first female graduates in the country.

Wanting to study medicine, Kadambini decided to enrol at the Calcutta Medical College after graduation. She was, however, believed to have been unable to receive the BMC certificate due to a shortage of a couple of marks. She did receive the GBMC (Graduate of Bengal Medical College) degree, though, in 1886. Thus, she became the first Indian woman to be allowed to practice Western medicine.

Around 1888, Kadambini started working at the Lady Dufferin Hospital for a monthly salary of 300 rupees. She had even gone to Nepal to treat British royalty. Along with pursuing medicine, she was also politically quite vocal and active. Around 1899, Kadambini was one of the first women delegates elected to the Fifth Session of the Congress in Bombay and the next year, she won to become the first women speaker at the Congress.

She also served as the president of the Transvaal Indian Association, founded by Gandhiji’s colleague Henry Pollock. She was a member of the Women’s Conference held in Calcutta and even presided over the General Brahmo Samaj session in Calcutta.

Around 1883, Kadambini married Dwarakanath Ganguly (thus the change in name from Kadambini Bose to Kadambini Ganguly in many documents). Dwarakanath Ganguly was a Bengali Brahmo reformer, educator, journalist, and pioneer of women’s rights in British India.

She was a mother to eight children and is often said to have been deft in needlework. She became a practising doctor while equally devoting herself to family and household affairs, an action which was deemed impossible by many in the era.

Despite having being burdened with domestic chores, like most women of that time, Kadambini still managed to smash the glass ceilings and societal stereotypes in both her professional and personal life.
A name which should not be forgotten in the course of time, Dr Kadambini is a reason many of us are able to pursue our passion — in medicine and in life.

fullParagraphs: Billionaire Deepinder Goyal has begun selling Temple, a temple-attached wearable he says can monitor brain health and ageing by measuring cerebral blood flow outside the lab. Critics and doctors question the device’s medical claims, noting the evidence is preliminary, not peer-reviewed, and its core metric—the Brain Flow index—remains controversial amid concerns over links to longevity or cognitive outcomes

Billionaire entrepreneur Deepinder Goyal, co-founder of Zomato and Blinkit, has announced the commercial availability of Temple, a wearable monitoring device that he claims could become “Humanity’s last personal device”.

A graduate in Computer Science and Mathematics from the Indian Institute of Technology Delhi, Mr. Goyal has no academic background in medical sciences or biological research. His claims have drawn criticism from doctors, including social media influencer and physician Cyriac Abby Philips (LiverDoc), who has described the device as a “scam”.

fullParagraphs: Megaspeed International has come under the scanner after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s alleged affair with Alice Huang, a woman accused of being a Chinese spy.

Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based cloud computing firm, is in the spotlight after the alleged extramarital affair of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang with one of the company’s former executives, Alice Huang. Ms Huang is accused of being a Chinese spy.

According to its website , Megaspeed is an Nvidia cloud partner in the Asia-Pacific region and a core business partner of Nvidia’s computing power cloud business. It adds that “we provide privatized, customized computing power product services covering NVIDIA’s entire GPU product line.”

A Reuters report says that Megaspeed International was incorporated in 2015 as 7Road International before changing its name to Megaspeed International in March 2023. It adds that the company is wholly owned by Singapore-registered Swiftdata, incorporated in October 2023, which says providing hosting services by non-data centers is its principal activity.

Reuters adds that Megaspeed’s assets increased sharply to $3 billion in 2024 from $33 million in 2023, its business filings showed. It reported an after-tax loss of $20 million ‌in ⁠2024, versus a loss of $21,283 a year earlier, while revenue jumped to $294 million from zero. Its cash flow statement showed $844,555 went to investing activities in 2024, after financing activities brought in cash of $10 million the previous year.

According to the company’s LinkedIn , it has around 2-10 employees and 23 associated members. The interactive map by LinkedIn shows that Megaspeed has offices in Iskandar Puteri, Malaysia; Senayan City, Indonesia; and is headquartered in the Central Region of Singapore.
Map showing the alleged locations of Megaspeed International | Photo Credit: Screengrab from LinkedIn

Washington has restricted the export of Nvidia’s most cutting-edge silicon chips to China, citing national security concerns. The move is also seen as a measure to stay ahead in the field of artificial intelligence.
The New York Times has reported that the U.S. government has been probing Megaspeed since 2024 over its potential steering of Nvidia chips to China.
All of this, combined with the allegations of Ms Huang being a Chinese spy, has triggered speculation over Megaspeed’s involvement in the alleged chip transfer to China.

As per an AFP report, in 2025, Bloomberg News also reported on the Singaporean probe into Megaspeed over the alleged smuggling of Nvidia chips to China. According to AFP , Megaspeed retorted in December of the same year, saying that Bloomberg’s reporting “contains misleading information and incorrect insinuations, including suggestions that we may have been involved in illegal chip transfers”.

articles.title: Akhilesh vows to make Ayodhya ‘global capital of Sanatan pilgrimage’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Alleging that devotees had been hurt by the "theft from the Ram temple", Akhilesh Yadav said his party would also introduce a transparent system for the temple to restore public confidence

Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav has promised to develop Ayodhya with world-class infrastructure and transform it into the "global capital of Sanatan pilgrimage" if his party comes to power in Uttar Pradesh after the elections next year.

In a post on X late Monday night (November 9, 2026), Mr. Yadav, who prominently raised the alleged donation theft at the Ram temple in June, said his party was committed to restoring Ayodhya's dignity and improving its local economy, which he claimed had been affected by a decline in the number of devotees visiting the holy city.

Alleging that devotees had been hurt by the "theft from the Ram temple", the former Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister said his party would also introduce a transparent system for the temple to restore public confidence.
"We will provide world-class infrastructure and make Ayodhya the 'global capital of Sanatan pilgrimage'," Mr. Yadav said.

He also promised to promote traditional boating in Ayodhya to benefit local boatmen and revive the association between Lord Ram and Nishadraj, the king of Shringverpur and the leader of the Nishada, a tribal community, in the Ramayana.

Mr. Yadav alleged that the BJP was attempting to undermine this relationship because it did not want people to remember the bond between Lord Ram and the PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) communities.
He further promised to free Ayodhya from outside contractors and order an investigation into land transactions in the city.
Alleging irregularities in circle rates and collusion between BJP leaders and corrupt officials, he said those involved would be held accountable and their alleged ill-gotten wealth investigated.
Mr. Yadav also promised to provide ration beneficiaries with oil and ghee to meet their nutritional requirements.

The SP would ensure that nobody was humiliated or assaulted in the name of collecting oil, Mr. Yadav said, referring to incidents of the poor collecting leftover oil from diyas at the Saryu river ghats in Ayodhya after the grand Deepotsav celebrations.

articles.title: Karnataka Industries Minister blames Gadkari for ‘ethanol blending crisis’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: ‘They [the Centre] refuses to believe me when I speak the truth about ethanol blending; let them ask sugar industry leaders such as Murugesh Nirani and Prabhakar Kore’ said M.B. Patil

Karnataka Industries Minister M.B. Patil on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) accused Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari of being primarily responsible for the crisis that has arisen due to allowing of ethanol to be blended with petrol allegedly beyond the prescribed limits.
Speaking to media persons here, Mr. Patil demanded a comprehensive investigation into the matter.

“They [the Centre] refuses to believe me when I speak the truth about ethanol blending. Let them ask sugar industry leaders such as Murugesh Nirani and Prabhakar Kore. Did we not send petrol samples to the Union government’s own laboratories for testing? Why should there be any doubt about the test results?” he wondered.
The Minister also said ethanol stocks at sugar factories have exceeded their storage capacity.

“The problem is not confined to Karnataka; Maharashtra is facing the same situation. The position is relatively better only in Uttar Pradesh. The Union government encouraged excessive ethanol production but failed to ensure adequate procurement. The scheme should initially have been introduced on a pilot basis in four or five districts to assess its advantages and disadvantages. Instead, Mr. Gadkari introduced the ethanol-blending system abruptly, resulting in the present crisis,” Mr. Patil alleged.

articles.title: NMDC said to be in talks with Russia’s Rosatom over lithium investments
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Rosatom and Russian miner Nornickel, however, are developing the country’s largest lithium deposit through their PolarLithium joint venture, with commercial production expected to begin by 2030

Indian state-run miner NMDC Ltd. is in talks with Russia’s Rosatom to invest in Russian lithium projects, three people familiar with the matter said, as India steps up efforts to secure supplies of the metal for its battery and EV industries.
NMDC officials visited Russia last month for a conference and also held talks with state nuclear firm Rosatom, two of the people said.

The third person, who also confirmed that company officials had met with Rosatom, said NMDC was keen to explore lithium mining and processing opportunities in Russia and had also held discussions with other Russian companies.

All three people, who asked not to be named as the talks were confidential, said discussions between NMDC and Rosatom remain preliminary. A Rosatom spokesperson did not address Reuters queries about the meetings last month but said the Russian company was not currently engaged in talks with NMDC.

NMDC did not respond to a Reuters request for comment. NMDC said last year it was exploring acquisition opportunities for critical minerals in Africa, Australia and South America as part of its global mineral diversification strategy.
It has formed a 12-member team to carry out due diligence on potential critical mineral assets, one of the people said.

Last week, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s cabinet approved an incentive policy worth ₹28.14 billion ($297million) to boost domestic processing of lithium and nickel. India’s domestic processing capacity for critical minerals, including lithium, remains at a nascent stage, the government has said, leaving it heavily dependent on imports.
It currently meets lithium demand primarily through imports from China, Vietnam and Ecuador.

Despite possessing large lithium reserves, Russia currently has no commercial production. Rosatom and Russian miner Nornickel, however, are developing the country’s largest lithium deposit through their PolarLithium joint venture, with commercial production expected to begin by 2030.

articles.title: Myanmar army seizes key resistance headquarters and 10 bases held by opposition, state media says
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Myanmar's military has seized a key resistance military command headquarters and 10 other bases in the south of the country, state media reported on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), marking a new gain by the army in the civil war as it seeks control of regions long held by resistance forces.
The capture of the bases in the jungle along the border between Mon state and the Bago region marks the latest setback suffered by pro-democracy armed groups and ethnic militias fighting the army.
The reported capture could not be independently confirmed because the military does not allow journalists free access to the area, but the claim has not been challenged.

The military-backed government, which took office in April following controversial elections earlier this year, has stepped up activity in recent months on the ground and with airstrikes to retake areas controlled by the People's Defense Force, the armed wing of the major opposition National Unity Government, and ethnic militias that have been fighting the central government for greater autonomy for decades.
The PDF emerged after the army seized power from the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi in February 2021 and has since formed loose alliances with ethnic militias fighting the military.

A report in the state-run Myanma Alinn newspaper on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) said the army captured 11 bases operating in the jungle area straddling the border between Mon and Bago during a six-day operation that began a week ago.

The captured positions included the special region command headquarters of the NUG and a battalion headquarters of the Karen National Liberation Army, the armed wing of the Karen National Union, a major Karen ethnic rebel group.
The paper published photos showing soldiers who captured the bases alongside ammunition seized during the operation.
Small arms, ammunition supplies, vehicles, drones and computers were captured after four armed engagements, the report said, adding that the military would continue security operations in the region.
The NUG and KNU did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

articles.title: Israeli forces shoot dead 14-year-old in West Bank: Palestinian officials
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Israeli forces shot dead a 14-year-old in the occupied West Bank, Palestinian officials said, with Israel saying it was responding to stone-throwing.
Moutaz Eyad Daghlas was killed in Burqa, northwest of Nablus, late on Monday (November 9, 2026), the Palestinian health ministry said.

The Palestine Red Crescent Society said its teams treated two people with gunshot wounds and took them to hospital, but that Israeli forces blocked access to a third wounded person and detained three volunteer paramedics.
The Israeli military, asked by AFP about the incident, said on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) it had acted to "thwart stone-hurling and terrorist attacks" in the area.

"The soldiers identified several terrorists who intended to hurl stones at a highway used by Israeli vehicles. This was in an area where stones have recently been hurled at Israeli vehicles," the military said.
"The soldiers responded by firing towards them in order to remove the threat."
Israeli forces have routinely opened live fire on Palestinians including minors who throw stones in the West Bank, which Israel has controlled since 1967.
The Israeli human rights group B'Tselem said Israeli forces killed at least 241 children or teenagers in the territory between the October 7, 2023 attack by Gaza-based Hamas and late June this year.

Violence has increased in recent weeks, especially in the run-up to Israel's October 27 election, before which Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had sought to appeal to hardline settlers in the West Bank.
On October 23, Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers at a checkpoint near Hebron before being killed by Israeli forces, who later responded with a major operation in the flashpoint city.

articles.title: New Israeli parliament to take aim at Netanyahu as Eisenkot seeks government
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Israel's new parliament convened on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) with plans to take aim immediately at caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, as his rival Gadi Eisenkot vowed to quickly cobble together a new government.

Mr. Eisenkot, leading a broad left-to-right bloc, will control the agenda from the outset in the new parliament with the help of Israeli-Arab parties, although neither he nor the right-wing Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving Prime Minister, hold a majority on their own.

"I am committed in this complex situation to form a national-emergency government as quickly as possible," Eisenkot, a 66-year-old former military chief who only recently entered politics, said before his swearing-in.
President Isaac Herzog, ceremonially opening the session, called on all sides to work together and avoid a fresh election in a deeply polarised country weary from three years of war.
"Nearly 80% of the people went to the polls and elected you. You must do everything to avoid a repeat election," Mr. Herzog said.
"Reach out a hand for compromise, even between rivals."

Mr. Eisenkot's allies hope to use their newfound legislative power to move rapidly on key priorities, including a commission to investigate security failures under Netanyahu that allowed the Hamas attack on October 7, 2023, the deadliest day in Israel's history.
ALSO WATCH Israel’s Eisenkot invites Netanyahu to join government under his leadership

Mr. Herzog on Sunday (November 8, 2026) gave Mr. Eisenkot the initial mandate to form a government, starting the clock for him to piece together a coalition within 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension.

Hours before the opening of the Parliament, known as the Knesset, Mr. Eisenkot's party announced agreements on key people to replace allies of Mr. Netanyahu, who has been in and out of office for nearly 20 years.

articles.title: EU climate chief Wopke Hoekstra warns 'expectations low' from COP31 summit
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: "If indeed we manage to make electrification the sole focus, or close to the sole focus of the COP, I think we have a chance to deliver on something that is truly meaningful," Wopke Hoekstra said

The European Union ’s (EU) top climate official admitted on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) that expectations were "low" from the COP31 summit in Turkiye, while holding out hope for "meaningful" progress on the topic of clean electricity.

"Expectations are low — that's just a reflection of reality," European Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra told a group of reporters including from AFP , arguing that electrification should be the core focus of the United Nations climate talks .
"If indeed we manage to make electrification the sole focus, or close to the sole focus of the COP, I think we have a chance to deliver on something that is truly meaningful," he said.

The European commissioner will travel to the Turkish resort of Antalya on Monday (November 9, 2026) for the talks which run until November 20. Mr. Hoekstra voiced hope that setting an electrification target would be "at the heart" of the summit conclusions, adding: "Of course, the cleaner that electrification is, the better it is."
ALSO WATCH COP31: Can negotiators finally deliver results? | The Hindu explains

Host nation Turkiye is inviting countries to join a voluntary "electrification" pledge to raise the share of global energy demand met by electricity from around 20% today to 35% by 2035. But the EU's call for "clean" electrification could spark debate over the role of oil, gas and coal in the Turkish proposal.
Observers expect few major breakthroughs from COP31 as countries grapple with an oil price shock and geopolitical tensions fuelled by the U.S. war with Iran and Russia's conflict in Ukraine.
The talks are also missing a major player since U.S. President Donald Trump who pulled Washington out of the Paris climate agreement has not sent officials to the talks.

"The larger picture is that the geopolitics of the times we live in are extremely complicated," said Mr. Hoekstra, who acknowledged that a string of recent COP meetings had been "underwhelming in terms of their delivery".
"There are substantial questions to be asked on how fit for purpose this design actually still is, with its unanimity" system that does not always deliver "what is actually needed," he said.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Amid a nationwide outcry over electoral malpractices, with fresh evidence emerging every day, the BJP government in Maharashtra has gone a step further in overturning a popular mandate through an executive fiat. It approved changing the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act through an ordinance on November 4 — which the Governor promulgated on November 6 — with the immediate effect of facilitating the takeover of the Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers’ Union, popularly known as Gokul Dairy , by the BJP and its allies. A Congress-led panel won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the board of the cooperative on October 19. Gokul, which is one of Maharashtra’s most influential cooperative institutions, has an annual turnover of around ₹4,000 crore and is linked to several lakh milk producers in western Maharashtra. The BJP had set its eyes on the cooperative sector as yet another arena of its political dominance, creating a Ministry of Cooperation under Home Minister Amit Shah. While that plan of controlling cooperatives continues to play out through various means, the overturning of an election clearly won by the Congress-led Opposition marks a new level of brazenness by the BJP, and of the impunity its actions continue to receive from the judiciary.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: This year’s Booker Prize betrays an anxiety about AI’s place in society

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A defining feature of the world today is that knowledge is proliferating and societies are struggling to agree on what is happening. AI models have significantly catalysed this devolution, allowing bad actors to flood spaces ranging from the research literature to public airwaves with questionable information, and drawing the attention of governments worldwide to the security implications of such a potent technology. The Booker Prize for M. John Harrison’s The End of Everything , a novel about a sense-defying alien invasion and the unsettling prospect of un-understandability it confronts humans with, effectively acknowledges the centrality of the AI question both through the book’s substance and the judges’ choice. A consequence of rampant AI use has been an assault on people’s attention span as well as the ability to make sense of new claims, so much so that reliable, verifiable meaning has become a premium entity. The novel, on the other hand, attempts to diagnose a post-meaning world in which people are only left to look inward. The Prize is also a long-overdue victory for the merits of science fiction, a genre that Harrison helped shape from the late 1960s, and one that English literature’s top honours have repeatedly overlooked. That said, the novel itself is far from being its best example, including because Harrison’s diagnosis lets technology and the practice of power off the hook for their failures.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: award-winning books / books and publishing / Artificial Intelligence

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Exclusion of creamy layer is essential, but must be done consistently

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: India’s federal structure could have benefited from the Kurian Committee

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: By abruptly disbanding the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee on Union-State Relations and handing over its task to the Tamil Nadu State Law Commission, the C. Joseph Vijay government appears to have succumbed to the political impulse to reverse earlier decisions rather than being guided by any compelling rationale or necessity. This gains credence from the very grounds cited. The committee executed its mandate with scholarly rigour, seen in Part I of its report that was submitted to the then M.K. Stalin government in February. Citing the Committee’s basic character of being a “non-statutory body” is unconvincing, particularly when the Law Commission itself is established only through “executive order”. There is also no public evidence of State Law Commissions having examined or addressed issues concerning Union-State relations. The mandate “to suggest ways and means for the inter-State relations and Centre-State relations”, constitutes only one part of the broader terms of reference of the State Law Commission, reconstituted in August. Given the commission’s wider responsibilities, successive State governments had constituted high-level committees to examine conflicts involving Concurrent List subjects and recommend specific remedies. It is through such recommendations that Tamil Nadu enacted certain pieces of legislation to overcome limitations imposed by central laws, including the provision of horizontal reservation in professional course admissions for disadvantaged students. Therefore, the State’s other argument of “similarity or overlap” in the “nature and scope of the functions” entrusted to the Committee and the Commission, does not withstand close scrutiny.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Any regulation of crackers needs strict enforcement at all levels

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The two Deepavali nights following the Supreme Court’s (SC) temporary relaxation of the cracker ban , played out predictably. The Air Quality Index (AQI) in several north Indian cities — already ‘poor’ and ‘very poor’ in the first week of November — was ‘severe’ on Deepavali night . Several air sensors — maintained by various organisations — reported PM2.5 in Delhi and its outskirts, exceeding 1,000 by Deepavali night. In this context, the SC’s order last week regarding crackers bears revisiting. While stating it was aware of the consequences of emissions from crackers, the Court has been waiting for quantitative evidence on the health and environmental effects of emissions from Deepavali celebrations. Such direct, causative evidence is almost impossible to furnish. Slackening winds and post-monsoon atmospheric dryness are known to trap the latent particulate matter from vehicles, industries, construction dust and stubble burning. Crackers are only an additional element that further degrades an already vitiated air. Delhi’s five-day average AQI rose from approximately 298 before Deepavali to 358 afterwards in 2024, 259 to 315 in 2025 and from 350 to 376 in 2026. While the timing of these spikes is consistent with a contribution from firecrackers, their precise share of overall pollution cannot be isolated from other emissions and meteorological influences. An absolute ban would encourage “illegal crackers from across the border,” the Court was told. Cracker season begins a fortnight before Deepavali and therefore an earlier decision by the Court regarding its permissibility would have given stockists time to better dispense ‘green’ crackers.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Editorial Context: Cracker conundrum: On need for strict enforcement of cracker ban. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.
